_what: Hand corrections to compiled pack data, declared one row at a time with a reason each.
_why: Pack data lives in binary LevelDB. A change to it shows up in no diff, survives into every future release, and is invisible to review — so the only honest record of a hand-edit is one written down beside it. Each fix names the exact value it expects to find before it writes: a fix whose `from` no longer matches is REFUSED, not forced, because that means somebody changed it since and the reason below may no longer hold.  A FIX MUST DESCRIBE ONLY WHAT IT EDITS (3.519.0). 51 fixes here set ONE warp's `mods` but declared the whole `system.warps` ARRAY as their from/to. Every one of them was already applied and correct, and every one became a landmine: the moment a later release touched a DIFFERENT warp on the same spell, the fix reported that somebody had changed its target and refused. Two went off in a single run while the range channel was being built. They now name `system.warps.<i>.mods`. The 141 fixes that genuinely author a whole array still declare the whole array, which is correct - the rule is that the declaration matches the edit, not that arrays are forbidden.
_howToApply: node tools/apply-data-fixes.mjs [--dry-run]. Idempotent — a fix already applied reports as such and writes nothing.

fixes.name: Chain
fixes.reason: The printed Goods table gives Chain a Size of 'S/2h'. That notation appears exactly twice in the whole rulebook and is explained nowhere, but Brand — the only other entry carrying it, as 'S/1h' — has heldHands 1, which reads the '/1h' as a hand requirement. On that precedent '/2h' means two hands, and Chain was set to require none. It is ten feet long and rated to a 2,000 lb load, so two hands is also the sensible reading. Confirmed with Graham on 23 August 2026 before applying.

fixes.name: Earth Sense
fixes.reason: Earth Sense reads, in full: 'You gain Tremorsense.' The Tremorsense ability exists in the abilities pack and declares its own sense block (secondary, tactile), so granting it gives the character the sense on their sheet, in the senses list and in every reader of system.details.senses. Before this the feat carried only a printed note and handed over nothing — a character with Earth Sense had no Tremorsense anywhere in the system. This is the grant route Graham confirmed on 23 August as the right one for a feat that hands over an ability, and it is the same shape Monstrous Vision already uses for Darkvision.

fixes.name: Pack Instinct
fixes.reason: Pack Instinct reads 'You gain the Pact Attack creature ability', and the ability block printed immediately beneath it is headed PACK ATTACK. 'Pact' is a typo in the rulebook — it occurs once, against two occurrences of 'Pack Attack' — and the abilities pack carries Pack Attack with the matching text. Granting it hands the character the creature ability the feat names. NOTE WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: the Pack Attack ability itself carries no effects and no flags, so the extra 1d6 precision damage when two allies are in reach is text on the sheet rather than arithmetic. That is a separate piece of work on the ability, not on this feat, and granting the ability is the correct first half regardless.

fixes.name: Deific Presence
fixes.reason: The printed entry carries TWO target lines: "Range touch; Targets 1 creature" and "Area 40-foot burst (B); Targets any number of creatures". Graham ruled on 25 August 2026 that the first line is an error and should be ignored — the spell is the 40-foot burst affecting any number of creatures, which is what the pack already had for area and targets. The stray "touch" range came from the erroneous line and is cleared here. Deific Presence is a burst centred on the caster; it has no touch range.

fixes.name: Magnificent Dawn
fixes.reason: The book prints "Saving Throw see below" because the save genuinely differs by creature type: every creature makes a Reflex save against blinding, and for Ooze and Undead the same roll is ALSO a Basic save against 100 Essence damage. The pack named it Reflex, which is right for most creatures and wrong for the two that matter. Graham ruled on 25 August 2026 to leave this one manual and NOT state a save, so the engine rolls nothing rather than rolling the wrong thing for an Undead. Cleared deliberately — a blank here is a declared refusal, not a lost field.

fixes.name: Neutralise Poison
fixes.reason: REVERSING A FIX THAT WAS WRONG. On 25 August 2026 I set Neutralise Poison’s area to "10-foot radius" believing the rulebook printed it. It does not. The book’s entry for NEXUS OF ELEMENTAL ENERGY merges its trait line into the same <h3> as its name and PP cost, unlike every other entry, so the parser did not recognise it as a heading and absorbed its whole stat block into the PRECEDING spell — Neutralise Poison. The value written in was Nexus’s. Neutralise Poison prints only Tradition, Cast, Range and Targets; it has no area at all. Caught by verify-spell-book-fields once the parser was corrected, which is the check doing exactly what it was built for.

fixes.name: Orientate

to.note: (to navigate from where you cast it)

to.text: You sense which way north lies from your current position.

fixes.reason: Printed in full: "You sense the direction of north from your current position and gain a +1-status bonus with any checks made to navigate from your current location." Both halves are now carried. THE SKILL IS A JUDGEMENT AND IS FLAGGED: the book says "checks made to navigate" without naming a skill, and the system has both Survival and Nature. Survival is the navigation skill and is used here; if Graham rules that Nature should also qualify, this fix gains a second bonus entry rather than being rewritten. The note carries the north-sensing half, which is a real effect rather than flavour.

to.note: (while you do not close with enemies)
(while you do not close with enemies)
(while you do not close with enemies)
(while you do not close with enemies)

to.text: The bonuses apply only so long as the target does not move closer to an enemy on its turn, or moves at least 5 feet away from an adjacent one — judged at the table, since the system does not watch how a creature spent its movement.

fixes.reason: Printed: "...it gains a +1 status bonus to its DB, and a +1 status bonus on Saving Throws." FOUR ENTRIES BECAUSE THE SLOT VOCABULARY HAS NO COMBINED SAVE: bonusTargetFor maps fortitude/reflex/will to system.combat.saves.<slot> individually, so "Saving Throws" is three effects rather than one. THE CONDITION IS NOT AUTOMATED AND SAYS SO. The bonuses hold only while the target does not close with enemies, and nothing in this system watches how a creature spent its movement. The note states that in the book's own terms rather than letting the effects apply unconditionally in silence — half a rule applied and declared beats half a rule applied quietly.

fixes.name: Stabilise
fixes.reason: Stabilise imported with an empty effects array, so casting it printed its text and changed nothing — the Dying Check at the end of the target's turn ran exactly as if the spell had not been cast. The printed effect is 'The target's Dying condition does not increase at the end of their turn', which is a clamp on the Dying Check's delta, not a modifier on any value the sheet holds. The new 'marker' effect kind (module/magic/markers.mjs) is what carries it: the cast leaves a flagged effect on the target, and documents/combat.mjs spends it the next time the check would raise Dying. Target is 'targets' because the spell's own Targets line reads '1 creature with the Dying condition' — it is cast on somebody else, at 30 feet.

fixes.name: Light
fixes.reason: Light imported with no effects, so casting it printed its text and changed nothing — the illumination ladder never moved. The `light` effect kind added at 3.396.0 attaches the source to the target and moves with it (Graham's ruling, 25 August 2026). Target is 'targets' because the spell is cast on an object at touch range, held by you or a willing ally; the token carrying it is what the light rides.

fixes.name: Dancing Lights
fixes.reason: Dancing Lights imported with no effects. Target is 'self', not 'targets': the spell prints no Targets line at all — it creates four spheres that must stay within a 10-foot radius of each other and wink out if they leave the caster's range, and you move them when you Sustain. They follow the caster, so the caster is what they attach to. Cap is 7 rather than 8 because the spell says the spheres shed 'the same amount of light as a torch', and Graham ruled on 25 August that the torch comparison carries the torch's cap.

fixes.name: Continual Light
fixes.reason: Continual Light imported with no effects. Cast on an object, so 'targets'. Cap 7 by the same torch-comparison ruling as Dancing Lights — the base spell prints no cap of its own. Note the spell's warping option '+2 PP: +1 illumination level (max 9)' is NOT this entry's cap; a first pass at the harness read that clause as the base spell's ceiling and reported 9, which is why verify-light-sources now stops parsing at the Warping Options boundary.

fixes.name: Ghostly Lanterns
fixes.reason: Ghostly Lanterns imported with no effects. Target is 'self': the spell summons 1d6 figures that 'form a 10 foot circle around you and move with you' unless you Sustain to reposition them, so the caster is the bearer. Three steps, max 8, both printed.

fixes.name: Detect Life
fixes.reason: The spell imported with no effects, so casting it printed its text and granted nothing. Its printed effect is 'This acts as a Tertiary Sense using your Power Manipulation skill in place of Perception checks', which the new `sense` effect kind grants for the duration as a real ability item carrying a creatureAbility sense block — the same route natural attacks and breath weapons already use, so senses.mjs needed no change and the existing grantedItems hook removes it when the spell ends. The range is NOT stored: senseRangeFeet derives a tertiary sense as 30 feet plus 5 per Wisdom off whoever holds it. Target is 'self' because neither spell prints a Range or Targets line — the caster gains the sense. No modality is recorded, matching Life Sense and Blight Sense, where the book names no organ and the existing code is explicit about not inventing one; the consequence is that no Enhanced feat doubles it, which is intended. `rollWith` is displayed, not applied: nothing in this system rolls a check for a sense, so there is no Perception check to substitute into.

fixes.name: Guidance
fixes.reason: Guidance imported with no effects, so casting it printed its text and left nothing on the target. Its printed effect is a +1 status bonus 'to one attack roll, saving throw, or skill check the target attempts before the duration ends. If the target uses the bonus, the spell ends.' That is exactly a marker: a flag a rule elsewhere reads and spends, which is the mechanism built for Stabilise at 3.395.0. The card offer in dice/check-card-interactions.mjs finds it on the target's next attack, save or skill card, spends it once, and stamps the hour's immunity the spell also prints. Target is 'targets' because the spell has Range 30 feet and Targets 1 creature — it is cast on somebody else. The bonus is NOT an ordinary `bonus` effect: applyBonusEffect writes into a named pool and would hand the target a standing +1 to all three kinds of roll, where the spell grants one, once, on a roll of their choosing.

fixes.name: Tanglefoot

from.text: A sticky vine makes a Grapple (attack action) using your Spellcraft check at -4. The effect ends at the start of your next turn.

fixes.reason: Tanglefoot carried a `note` effect describing its own rule in prose — automation that is really a reminder, which is what this chapter has been removing. Its printed text is 'Use your Spellcraft result at -4 to perform a grapple action against the target', so the new `maneuver` effect kind rolls Spellcraft with the spell's -4 against the target's Fortitude DC (the DC the Grapple action itself names) and applies whatever that action's own outcome table says for the degree rolled. Nothing about grabbing is written here: basicActionConditionEffects owns the outcomes, which matters because Graham corrected grapple's critical in August against a typo in the printed book, and this spell inherits that correction without anyone remembering it should. Graham ruled on 25 August 2026 that the grapple size penalty applies ON TOP of the spell's -4, so a Medium caster tangling a Huge creature is at -8; that comes from MANEUVER_SIZE_PENALTY, moved to combat/attack.mjs in this release so the spell and the action read one table.

fixes.name: Tanglefoot
fixes.reason: REVERTING MY OWN FIX FROM 3.401.1. I relabelled Tanglefoot from 'attack' to 'utility' to stop the cast workflow rolling a second, spurious spell attack that critically hit for 0 damage and rolled a critical injury. That stopped the symptom by lying about the spell: Tanglefoot IS an attack spell, and the book prints it as one. Graham ruled on 25 August 2026: 'Attack spells follow the same path as attack actions as a general rule. So if a spell emulates an attack action that does not inflict damage (grapple, shove etc), it should also inflict no damage. Also, such actions do not inflict criticals so the spells that emulate them should not either.' So the category stays 'attack' and the MECHANISM changes instead — a spell carrying a maneuver effect does not run the spell-attack and damage pipeline, because its maneuver check is its attack. That fix is general and reaches Spectral Grasp and Telekinetic Manoeuvre, which are the same shape and would have had the same bug.

fixes.name: Fear
fixes.reason: Fear printed five outcomes and the pack carried ONE, applied to whoever failed: 'Critical The target is unaffected. Success The target is frightened 1. Partial the target is frightened 2. Failure The target is frightened 3. Fumble The target is frightened 4 and fleeing for 1 round.' The flattened entry was wrong in BOTH directions — a target that SUCCEEDED took nothing where the book says frightened 1, and a target that FUMBLED took 3 rather than 4 and never fled. Each degree now carries its own entry, gated with onSave. CRITICAL IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT: 'the target is unaffected' means no effect, so no entry, and the absence is the rule rather than an omission. BLUNDER RIDES WITH FUMBLE because the resolution table has a degree below fumble that the spell text does not name, and leaving it out would make the worst possible roll apply nothing at all — the same 'rolling worse does less' shape corrected for Heroic at 3.403.0, mirrored.

fixes.name: Sudden Sickening
fixes.reason: Sudden Sickening printed four outcomes and the pack carried one: 'Critical The creature is unaffected. Success The creature is sickened 1. Failure The creature is sickened 2. Fumble The creature is sickened 3.' Same flattening as Fear — a target that succeeded took nothing where the book says sickened 1. The spell names no Partial, so partial rides with failure: a partial is a FAILED save and must not do less than nothing; grouping it with the nearest named failing outcome is the reading that keeps the ladder monotonic. Blunder rides with fumble for the same reason.

Book text — success: The target is unaffected. | partial: The target is stunned 1. | failure: The target is stunned 2. | fumble: The target is stunned 3.

fixes.from:
You speak a potent magical word that has the potential to deafen one creature of your choice, whether the creature can hear the word or not. The duration of the spell depends upon the targets saving throw.

Success The target is deafened or 1 minute.

You speak a potent magical word that has the potential to deafen one creature of your choice, whether the creature can hear the word or not. The duration of the spell depends upon the targets saving throw.
Critical The target is deafened for 1 round.
Success The target is deafened for 1 minute.
Failure The target is deafened for 10 minutes.
Fumble The target is deafened permanently.

Warping Options:
+4 PP: the spell effects all creatures in a 20 feet radius.
fixes.reason: Transcription typo. All three timed rungs read "The target is deafened OR 1 round / 1 minute / 10 minutes" where the book means "FOR". The line immediately above them says "The duration of the spell depends upon the targets saving throw", so those rungs ARE durations and "or" is a keystroke slip repeated three times. Corrected on all three; the fumble rung ("deafened permanently") is left exactly as it stands. Found at 3.405.0 by tools/parse-degree-ladders.mjs, which refused the spell as unreadable prose — the refusal is what made anyone read the sentence.

fixes.name: Brain Lock
fixes.from:
You enter a battle of wills with the target in an attempt to hold them in place. The target must make a saving throw.
Critical The creature is unaffected and the spell ends.
Success The creature stunned 1.
Failure The creature is stunned 3.
Fumble As failure except the target is also paralyzed.
You must Sustain the Spell each round which forces the target to make a new saving throw.

Warping Options:
+1 PP: affect an additional target.

Failure The creature is stunned 3.

Warping Options:
+1 PP: affect an additional target.
fixes.reason: Transcription typo. The success rung reads "The creature stunned 1." with the verb missing; every other rung in the same ladder reads "The creature is ...". Found at 3.405.0 by tools/parse-degree-ladders.mjs, which refused the clause for having no readable verb. NOTE: this does not by itself make the spell wireable — its fumble rung says "As failure except the target is also paralyzed", a cross-reference to another rung that nothing can yet express, and it carries a Sustain clause besides.

fixes.name: Stone Shield

from.note: (cover from one chosen enemy until the start of your next turn)

to.text: If the opponent's attack misses you by 4 or less it strikes the shield instead. Hardness 8, Hits 15.

fixes.reason: A CORRECTION, NOT A WIRING. The row read {kind:"bonus", slot:"defence", value:4} with the scope that makes it correct sitting in a NOTE beside it: "(cover from one chosen enemy until the start of your next turn)". So the spell granted an unconditional +4 to DB against every attacker in the scene, where the book grants cover from ONE opponent. That is the difference between a modest 1-PP spell and the best defensive spell in the game, and it was live. Re-authored as a ward scoped to the chosen enemy by uuid; the parts of the note that really are GM-facing (the miss-by-4 rule, the shield's Hardness and Hits) are kept as a note, because those genuinely have no engine.

fixes.name: Anticipations
fixes.reason: Unwired. Printed: "For the duration of the spell you gain a +4 status bonus to DB against attacks made by the target." The caster benefits and the target is what the bonus is scoped against, so the effect targets self and the ward names the hostile target. DB only — the sentence says nothing about saves, so no save slots are declared.

fixes.name: Forbidding Ward
fixes.reason: Unwired — one of the last two PP 0 spells. Printed: "The target ally gains a +1-status bonus to DB and saving throws against the target enemy's attacks, spells, and other effects." Targets "1 ally and 1 enemy", so the effect targets the ALLY (target: "allies", split by disposition) and is scoped against the hostile target. All four slots because the sentence names DB and saving throws without qualifying which. The CL 10 increase to +2 is NOT wired here — caster-level modifications are a separate channel and inventing one inside a data fix would hide it.

fixes.name: Healing Earth
fixes.reason: Unwired — the last PP 0 spell. The spell makes a THING rather than granting a bonus, so it creates a piece of gear carrying the "Healer's Tools" trait: `consumeGearUse` already spends one use of the first equipped gear matching that trait on Treat Wounds, so the substitution happens in code that was already there rather than by teaching the Medicine workflow about spells. `target: "self"` because the earth is made at the caster's feet; it is ordinary gear from that moment and can be handed to anyone, which is Graham's ruling ("anyone who has it") and the book's own CL 5 wording ("grants ANYONE using it"). One use, ten minutes, and a recast reverts the earlier earth. The CL 5 +1 item bonus rides as a conditional on the item itself, scoped to Administer First Aid and Treat Wounds.

fixes.name: Daze
fixes.reason: Graham's ruling, 26 August 2026: "Daze should have base damage of 1d4." The pack said 1d6 while the printed text says "You cause 1d4 damage to the target" — the only one of the eleven baseDamage spells where the die and the book actually disagreed. `baseDamage` is the PER-DIE value the item sheet documents as "used for warping and criticals", so for the other ten (6d6 → 1d6, 2d10 → 1d10) it was right all along.

fixes.name: Daze
fixes.reason: The cast workflow rolls `system.damage.formula` and never reads `baseDamage`, so Daze — a PP 0 cantrip whose whole printed effect is 1d4 damage — dealt none. Type `mental`, from "you obscure the target's thoughts, causing a mental disruption" and matching the vocabulary already used by seven other spells. Category is `save`, so the Basic Save table scales it by degree. Found by tools/spell-automation-census.mjs, written after I told Graham PP 0 was finished when it was not.

fixes.name: Tame

to.text: Once the spell ends the target is temporarily immune for 1 day.

fixes.reason: Unwired, and the last PP 0 spell with real mechanics. "Improve the target's disposition towards you by one step... This effect lasts for the duration of the spell" — so a STEP rather than a charm, and TEMPORARY: it rides the spell's own 1 minute (10 at CL 5) in the temporary layer, leaving whatever the creature permanently thought untouched. The day's immunity afterwards is left as a note; temporary-immunity.mjs exists but nothing yet reads it for attitude, and wiring half of it would be worse than saying so.

fixes.name: Charm Kind

from.text: On a failed Will save the target's attitude becomes friendly toward you (helpful if already friendly) and it can't take hostile actions against you.

to.text: It can't take hostile actions against you, and the spell ends if you use hostile actions against it — both GM-adjudicated.

fixes.reason: Was a note that printed the rule and changed nothing. "The target's attitude becomes friendly toward you (helpful if already friendly)" is the charm sentence five spells share — neither a set (which would DOWNGRADE a helpful creature) nor a shift (which would leave a hostile one merely unfriendly). Temporary, on the spell's printed 10 minutes.

fixes.name: Charm Animal

from.text: On a failed Will save the animal's attitude becomes friendly toward you (helpful if already friendly) and it can't take hostile actions against you.

to.text: It can't take hostile actions against you, and the spell ends if you use hostile actions against it — both GM-adjudicated.

fixes.reason: As Charm Kind; the spell's own duration is 1 hour, which the per-effect duration reader picks up without this row saying anything.

fixes.name: Charm Undead

to.text: It can't take hostile actions against you, and the spell ends if you use hostile actions against it — both GM-adjudicated.

fixes.reason: Unwired. Its ladder is explicit — critical and success are both "unaffected" (differing only in what the target believes, which is GM-facing), and only failure and worse charm it. Gated with onSave so a successful save takes nothing, which is the defect 3.404.0 existed to remove. Sustained, 1 minute.

fixes.name: Alluring Caress

to.text: It can't take hostile actions against you, and the spell ends if you use hostile actions against it — both GM-adjudicated.

fixes.reason: Unwired, and its two bad degrees differ: failure is the charm sentence ("friendly, or helpful if it was already friendly"), fumble is a flat "becomes helpful". Two gated rows rather than one, because they are genuinely different outcomes. 10 minutes (D).

fixes.name: Thrall

to.text: It can't take hostile actions against you, and the spell ends if you use hostile actions against it — both GM-adjudicated.

fixes.reason: Unwired. THREE DIFFERENT DURATIONS across its degrees — success 10 minutes, failure 24 hours, fumble unlimited — which is exactly what the per-effect duration mechanism from 3.405.0 was built for. The fumble row declares no duration and the spell's own is "varies", which parses to nothing, so it lands as a temporary attitude that never lapses. Critical is "unaffected" and so gates on nothing.

fixes.name: Veiled Presence
fixes.reason: Unwired. "+2 status bonus to Deception and Stealth checks" — two plain bonus rows, one per skill, because the pool is per-slot. Self, 1 minute. The rest of the spell (blending into a crowd) is narrative and stays so.

fixes.name: Physical Surge
fixes.reason: Unwired. "+10-foot status bonus to your Speed and a +2 status bonus to all Athletics checks." The Speed half is the first user of the movement slot added this release — before it, `bonusTargetFor("speed")` pointed at `system.combat.speed`, which no actor has, and this row would have applied nothing at all. The free Stride/Leap/Climb/Swim is an action grant and stays with the GM.

fixes.name: Fluidity

to.text: You ignore difficult terrain for the duration, and may Stride or Step as part of casting.

fixes.reason: Unwired. "+5-foot status bonus to your Speed" is a bonus; "ignore difficult terrain" has no engine to hang on and stays a note rather than being pretended at.

fixes.name: Quick Time
fixes.reason: Unwired. "Both you and all allies in the area gain a +10-foot status bonus to all Speeds." A 60-foot radius area spell, so the template already picks the recipients out; the row targets them. NOTE: the book says "all Speeds" and this grants land only — the movement slot map can express fly/swim/climb/burrow individually, but a single row cannot yet mean "every speed at once", and inventing four rows would claim a precision the mechanism does not have. Flagged rather than fudged.

fixes.name: Spirit Of The Hunt

to.text: Advantage on Search (Perception) checks for the duration.

fixes.reason: NOT wired to a bonus, deliberately. "Granting advantage on Search (Perception) checks" is ADVANTAGE, not a numeric bonus, and there is no spell-effect kind that grants a conditional. Left as a note that states the rule plainly; wiring it as a +N would be a different rule wearing this one's name. SUPERSEDED at 3.497.0: the note this fix wrote was replaced by a real scoped-advantage conditional. See spirit-of-the-hunt-advantage.

fixes.name: Quick Time
fixes.reason: Graham’s ruling, 26 August 2026: “Quick Time will affect any speeds that the character has (but only if they have them).” 3.410.0 granted land only and flagged the gap rather than fudging it; this replaces that with the `allSpeeds` slot, which resolves against the TARGET at apply time to however many positive movement speeds they actually have. A landbound human gains land; a dragon gains land, fly and swim; nobody gains a swim speed they never had.

fixes.name: Guidance

to.label: Guidance
to.spentNote: Temporarily immune to Guidance for 1 hour.

fixes.reason: MIGRATED, not rewired. Guidance was built at 3.400.0 as a bespoke marker with its own card button, its own hardcoded +1 and its own hardcoded label. Four PP 1 spells then turned out to share its shape exactly, and four more buttons would have been five copies of one idea. It is now the first HELD BONUS, with its printed hour of immunity expressed as a field rather than as code. Behaviour is unchanged: +1 status to one attack, save or skill check, spent from the card, immunity stamped on spend and not on apply.

fixes.name: Learned Council

from.text: One ally gains a +2 circumstance bonus to any one attack roll, saving throw, or skill check before the start of your next turn.

fixes.reason: Was a note. "The ally gains a +2 circumstance bonus on any attack roll, saving throw, or skill check made before the beginning of your next turn" is Guidance's shape at +2 and a different pool. No immunity — the spell prints none.

fixes.name: Weapon Surge

from.text: Your next Strike with the imbued weapon (before your next turn) gains +1 status to attack and deals an extra damage die.

fixes.reason: Was a note. "On your next Strike with that weapon before the start of your next turn, you gain a +1 status bonus to the attack roll." Narrowed to attack checks. NOTE: the spell says "with THAT weapon" and a posted check card does not name the weapon, so this reaches the next attack with any of them — flagged rather than fudged, and the remaining damage clause stays with the GM.

fixes.name: Wizard Strike
fixes.reason: Unwired. "The next time you make an attack check before the end of your next turn" — attack checks only, one use, spent from the card.

fixes.name: Physical Boost
fixes.reason: Unwired. "+1 status bonus to the next Constitution, Strength, or Dexterity based check." Scoped to ATTRIBUTE checks on those three, which is the narrow and defensible reading: a posted card reports a skill check by its SKILL key, so "a Strength based skill" is not identifiable from the card and claiming it would be a scope that matched by accident.

fixes.name: Quick Time

to.text: You and all allies in the area gain a +10-foot status bonus to all Speeds for 1 round. Speed bonuses are not yet automatable: movement is stored as a bare number, not a bonus pool, so a status bonus has nowhere to land. Apply by hand.

fixes.reason: REVERTED at 3.411.1, after live proof. 3.410.0 gave these a `speed` bonus slot and a check confirmed the path existed — it does, as the NUMBER 30. `applyBonusEffect` writes to `<target>.<bonusType>`, so the change landed on `movement.land.status`, a property on a number, and did nothing. One cast of Physical Surge showed it plainly: Athletics 0 → 2, land 20 → 20. Movement is not a bonus pool and no Speed bonus can land until it is. The working half of Physical Surge (Athletics) is kept; the speed halves become notes that say why, rather than automation that does not run.

fixes.reason: RESTORED at 3.412.0 on Graham’s ruling that movement can become a bonus pool. The speed halves were reverted to notes at 3.411.1 because each speed was a bare number and a typed bonus written to `movement.land.status` vanished — proved live, Athletics 0 → 2 while land stayed 20. to.text: A free Stride, Leap, Climb or Swim as you cast.

fixes.reason: RESTORED at 3.412.0 on Graham’s ruling that movement can become a bonus pool. The speed halves were reverted to notes at 3.411.1 because each speed was a bare number and a typed bonus written to `movement.land.status` vanished — proved live, Athletics 0 → 2 while land stayed 20. fixes.name: Loremasters Edge
fixes.reason: "Trigger: You attempt a Recall Knowledge check. You gain advantage on the check." One triggered check, then the spell ends — the held-bonus shape, with advantage as the payload instead of a number. Scoped by ACTION rather than by skill, because Recall Knowledge is rolled from several skills and the card carries actionKey.

fixes.name: Revelation Divine
fixes.reason: "Trigger: You attempt a Search (Perception) check, or a skill check to Recall Knowledge with a skill you're trained in. You gain advantage on the triggering check." Same mechanism as Loremasters Edge, two actions. The 'trained in' half is NOT expressed: the posted card does not carry proficiency, and a scope that silently never narrows is worse than one the GM applies knowingly — see the note effect.

fixes.name: Moment Of Fortune

to.label: Moment Of Fortune
to.spentNote: The spell ends. Only one Moment Of Fortune may run at a time — recasting it fades the previous one.

to.text: You may only have one Moment Of Fortune running at a time; casting it again fades the previous one.

fixes.reason: "When the target would attempt a saving throw, it can roll with advantage. Once it does this, the spell ends." The held-bonus mechanism already ends on spend. The one-instance-at-a-time clause is a NOTE, not automation: nothing in the system tracks a named spell's prior instance yet, and a note that says so beats a silent second instance.

fixes.name: Inspiration

to.label: Inspiration
to.spentNote: This cannot prevent an open-ended result.

to.text: Cannot prevent you from succumbing to an open ended result.

fixes.reason: "Trigger: you make a non-attack skill check. You may roll 1d6 and add it to the total result." The third held payload: a die rather than a flat number. checkTypes ['skill'] alone already excludes attacks, so the 'non-attack' half needs no extra axis. UNTYPED because the text names no bonus type, and untyped stacks — a typed guess would silently suppress it under an existing status bonus.

fixes.name: Luminous Flare

from.text: Fortitude: success → dazzled 1 round; failure → blinded 1 round + dazzled 1 minute (fumble: dazzled 1 hour). Blinded can be ended with a 1-AP rub-eyes Interact.

to.text: A 1 AP Interact action rubbing the eyes ends the blinded condition.

fixes.reason: THE SPELL effect-duration.mjs WAS WRITTEN FOR, still flattened. It shipped applying `blinded` with NO onSave and NO duration: successes took nothing (the book gives them dazzled 1 round), and failures were blinded PERMANENTLY, because the spell's own duration is blank and a blank duration means no timing at all. The printed ladder is now four rows with three different lengths. Only the four printed rungs are declared: `effectiveSaveDegree` maps partial to success and blunder to fumble before any effect is read, so listing them again would be two authors describing one rung.

fixes.name: Touch Of Obedience

to.duration: until the end of your current turn
until the end of your next turn

fixes.reason: A Will-save ladder whose three rungs differ in BOTH magnitude and length. It could not be written before 3.414.0: `parseSpellDuration` returned null for "until the end of your current turn" and "until the end of your next turn", and null means no timing, which `unreadableEffectDurations` rightly refuses to ship. Those phrases were readable all along in outcome-effects.mjs; uniting the two is what unblocked this. The spell's own duration field says "varies", which is exactly what a per-effect duration is for.

fixes.name: Enchanting Utterance

from.text: Will: success → the target takes -1 circumstance to attack & damage against you; failure → it can't take hostile actions against you; fumble → also stunned 1.

to.text: Failure or fumble: the target cannot take hostile actions against you for the duration.

fixes.reason: The first spell to use the mirror scope axis. The success rung is "-1 circumstance to attack rolls and -1 to damage rolls AGAINST YOU" — a penalty carried by the enemy that vanishes the moment they swing at somebody else, which is exactly what `targetUuids` was built to express and what a flat -1 could not. The FAILURE rung stays a note on purpose: "cannot take hostile actions against you" is a restriction on what a creature may DO, not a modifier on a roll, and nothing in the system yet forbids an action toward one named creature — a note that says so beats a silent nothing. The fumble's stunned 1 is a plain condition and is wired. SUPERSEDED at 3.493.0 by enchanting-utterance-failure-rung: this fix gave the spell its success and fumble rows and left the Failure outcome as prose inside an ungated note. That was harmless while an unnamed degree read upward to the milder neighbour; Graham's ruling of 4 September 2026 reversed the failing side, so a plain Failure fell to the Fumble rung and picked up stunned 1 — a condition the book gives only on a Fumble. The heir declares the Failure rung instead.

fixes.name: Arrow Of The Wild Hunt

to.label: Arrow Of The Wild Hunt
to.scope: ranged

fixes.reason: Silent, and one of the ten spells whose only record of damage sat in `baseDamage` — the field the item sheet documents as "used for warping and criticals" and which the cast workflow never rolls. "Make a ranged weapon Strike. On a hit, deal normal damage plus 1d6 force damage" is a SECONDARY packet on a Strike, which is the rune chapter's own mechanism, so it is declared as a rider and rolled by the same loop. `scope: "ranged"` because the spell says "ranged weapon Strike"; `once` because the arrow is loosed one time. The +4 PP ricochet stays a warp for the GM — a second Strike at the same MAP is an action, not a damage packet.

fixes.name: Talon Strike

from.text: Strikes with the target weapon deal +1d6 secondary slashing damage (warpable to 2d6).

to.label: Talon Strike
to.scope: any

fixes.reason: Note-only. "Your attacks with the target weapon ... inflicting 1d6 secondary slashing damage", Duration 1 minute — so `once: false`, and every Strike with that weapon carries it until the spell ends. `weaponScoped` because the spell targets "a weapon you are currently wielding": the applier asks which one when more than one is equipped, and refuses the effect out loud when none is. Left unscoped it would arm the whole armoury for a minute, which is a different spell. The +4 PP warp to 2d6 stays a warp.

fixes.name: Spoil The Profane

from.text: Make a weapon Strike; on a hit the target is also weakened 1 until your next turn (an opposed-aura target also takes 1d6 aligned damage).

to.label: Spoil The Profane
to.scope: any
to.against: a target with an opposing aura

fixes.reason: Note-only, and the spell is two rules in one sentence. The WEAKENED 1 is unconditional — "on a hit ... the target becomes weakened 1 until the beginning of your next turn" — and is applied. The 1d6 is conditional on the target having "an opposing aura", a phrase that appears in no module in this system; Radiant Aegis and Wellspring Of Valour are waiting on the same question. So it is declared `conditional` and PRINTED on the strike card rather than applied, which is exactly what the Bane and Aligned runes already do for the same reason: they "depend on WHO is being hit, which nothing here can know". Inventing an aura test to make the number land would be a rule wearing this spell's name. The +2 PP warp declares `damageDice: "1d6"` and reaches the die through the same `addDice` the heal rows use; the +3 PP weakened warp stays a warp.

fixes.name: Banish Fatigue

from.text: The target ignores 1 point of fatigue for the duration (warpable to more, or to remove it permanently).

to.text: +4 PP removes the fatigue permanently rather than suppressing it — apply that by hand.

fixes.reason: Note-only. "You reinvigorate the target causing them to ignore 1 point of fatigue for the duration" (1 hour) is a standing suppression, not a removal: the target still HAS the fatigue and ignores a point of it, which is exactly what the new `suppress` kind expresses — see conditions/suppression.mjs. The +2 PP warp is one more point and is a warp; the +4 PP warp REMOVES the fatigue permanently, which is a different operation from ignoring it and is left as a note for the GM rather than pretended at by a suppression that would end with the spell.

fixes.name: Confident Veil

from.text: Lowers your frightened by 1 now and reduces any new frightened by 1 for the duration; a fumbled fear save ends the spell and raises frightened by 1.

to.text: If you fumble a saving throw against fear while this runs, the spell ends and your frightened increases by 1.

fixes.reason: Note-only, and its first TWO printed clauses are one rule. "This lowers your existing frightened condition by 1, AND whenever you would normally become frightened during the spell's duration, effect is reduced by 1" — a standing -1 to the EFFECTIVE value of frightened does both, because it is not an event that fires once but a subtraction that is always true while the effect lives. One row, not two. The third clause — a fumbled fear save ends the spell and raises frightened by 1 — stays a NOTE: this system has no hook for "the save you just fumbled had the fear trait" (searched for before writing this), and inventing one to serve a single PP 1 spell would be a mechanism built in the wrong order.

fixes.name: Surge Of The Tempest
fixes.reason: The book says "The target must make a BASIC Reflex save to partially avoid the effects", and the pack said only "Reflex". `parseSpellDefence` reads the word "basic" out of this string to decide whether damage is scaled by degree — so as written the spell would have dealt full damage on a success. A one-word data fault that the damage repair below would otherwise have shipped on top of.

fixes.name: Surge Of The Tempest
fixes.reason: One of the ten spells whose only record of damage sat in `baseDamage`, the field nothing rolls. "The storm unleashes a surge of electrical energy, dealing 1d12 damage" now lives in `damage.formula`, where the cast workflow reads it. **`persistent` IS CLEARED, DELIBERATELY.** It held "1", and the book gives that persistent electricity only "in the event of a fumble" — but `system.damage.persistent` is printed unconditionally by the damage path, on every degree, with no gate of any kind. Filling the formula while leaving it would have handed every target of every cast a point of persistent damage the spell never grants. Moved to a note until a degree-gated persistent damage exists; the +2 PP warp that raises it is unaffected and stays a warp.

fixes.name: Surge Of The Tempest

from.text: 1d12 electricity (Basic Reflex). On a fumble the target is also dazzled 1 round and takes 1 persistent electricity.

to.text: On a fumble the target also takes 1 persistent electricity damage (+1 per 2 PP warped) — apply by hand.

fixes.reason: Note-only. The dazzled half is a plain degree-gated condition and is now wired the way Luminous Flare's ladder already is. The persistent half is NOT, and the reason is written beside the damage fix above: nothing in this system can make persistent damage depend on the save degree. Stated in a note that says what to do rather than dropped.

fixes.name: Vibrant Thorns

to.text: +4 PP: the damage increases by 1, or to 1d6 after you cast an essence spell — warped by hand.

fixes.reason: Silent. "Whenever a creature adjacent to you or a creature that hits you with an unarmed attack lands a melee blow, they suffer 1 piercing damage" is a rider on being HIT — the mirror of the strike riders built at 3.437.0, landing in the same function a few lines from the Vicious rune, which is the only other thing there that damages the person who swung. fixes.name: Wellspring Of Valour

to.text: Whenever an ally in the aura first takes damage each round, they regain 1d6 HP — apply by hand; the on-damage trigger is not yet automated.

fixes.reason: "You create an aura of vitality which grants allies a +1 status bonus to attack rolls vs any creatures of an opposed aura. Whenever an ally in the aura first takes damage each round, they regain 1d6 HP." The spell was SILENT — no effects, no damage, no named mechanism — and the first half was blocked on what an opposing aura is. Graham ruled on 31 August 2026 that an aura type IS the Aligned trait, and that a Balance-aligned character gains nothing from these spells deliberately. `opposedAura: true` marks the bonus as conditional so it is NOT written into the sheet total (which would raise it against everybody) but carried as a record the attack roll consults against this target — see magic/opposed-aura.mjs. THE HEAL STAYS A PRINTED NOTE: "first takes damage each round" is a new trigger (on-damage, once per round, per creature) and Vibrant Thorns is its precedent, but building it is a separate piece of work. Flagged rather than half-built, and the note says plainly that it is applied by hand.

fixes.name: Wellspring Of Valour
fixes.reason: "+4 PP: increase the bonus by +1 and the healing by 1d6." The bonus half rides the existing `bonusValue` key. NO `bonusMax` IS DECLARED because the book prints no ceiling for this one — unlike the radius warp beside it, which prints "max 50 feet". Inventing a cap would be a rule its author never wrote. THE HEALING HALF IS NOT DECLARED at all: the heal it would scale is itself still a printed note, so a mod key for it would scale nothing — and `aggregateWarpSelection` silently drops keys it does not list, which is the freezeMembership defect this project has now met twice. Both halves land together when the on-damage trigger is built.

fixes.name: Radiant Aegis
fixes.reason: "A halo of energy appears around which grants your allies a +1 status bonus to DB against attacks made by creatures with an opposing aura type to your own." The spell was SILENT. This is Inspire Defence's row exactly — {kind: bonus, target: targets, slot: defence, bonusType: status, value: 1} — plus `opposedAura: true`, which is what stops it being written into the DB total. A plain row would raise the ally's Defence against EVERY attacker, which is the Stone Shield defect: "cover from one chosen enemy" shipped once as an unconditional +4. Marked conditional, it rides the defence-DC channel instead and is consulted per attacker, against the caster's own opposites resolved at the cast. Graham ruled on 31 August 2026 that an aura type is the Aligned trait, and that a Balance-aligned caster gaining nothing is deliberate. NO NOTE IS ADDED for the condition: the cast card prints it from opposedAuraLine(), so a note would be a second place saying it.

fixes.name: Healer’s Grace
fixes.reason: "Whenever you cast a spell that possesses the Healing Trait, it is considered to be warped 2 PP higher at no extra PP cost." The spell was SILENT. NOTHING NEW WAS BUILT FOR IT: `warpFreeSchool` has carried exactly this rule since Powerful Illusion at 3.332.0, and its test is `spellTraits.includes(...)` — scoped by TRAIT despite the name — so the spell grants the same flag the Wizard feat does. `target: "self"` because the spell has no Targets line and its text is about the caster's own words. Reaches the 30 spells in the pack that carry the Healing trait. FOUND WHILE BUILDING IT: the free-warp channel's card note said "Powerful Illusion" for every source, hard-coded, so a Cleric under this spell would have been told a Wizard feat waived their PP; the note now names the grant, fixed at 3.447.0.

fixes.name: Healer’s Grace
fixes.reason: "+4 PP: increase the amount warped by healing spells by an additional 1 PP (max +4)." Rides the existing bonusValue/bonusMax keys, which the freeWarp effect now reads through `warpedBonusValue` — the one function every other warped bonus already asks. THE CAP IS READ AS THE TOTAL, not as a ceiling on the increase: Bless sells "+1 (max +4)" on a base of 1 and its cap is the total, so this reads the same way and Healer's Grace tops out at 4 PP of free warping rather than 6. Flagged as a reading rather than a quotation — the printed words carry both, and this is the one that matches the precedent beside it.

fixes.name: Inspire Competence
fixes.reason: "This counts as if you had taken an Aid action, using the result of the spell's check instead of a specific skill. The minimum bonus granted is +1." The spell was SILENT, and was blocked on what an Aid action IS — the system's only two Aid actions are combat ones (an attack roll vs Defence), while this aids a SKILL check. Graham gave the general rule on 31 August 2026: "one character must be appointed as the lead character. All other characters make an EASY Skill check using the Bonus Check Table. The resulting bonus is added as a CIRCUMSTANCE BONUS to the lead character's check." Everything follows from that sentence: the DC is levelDC(ally) at the Easy rung (-2), the table is buildOutcome's own, and the bonus is circumstance — so two Bards encouraging one ally do not stack. The spell's own "minimum +1" is a FLOOR on the table, which is the mirror of Counter Perform flooring at zero and recording nothing. Spent by the ally's next SKILL check in dice/check.mjs, the third spell to use that road.

fixes.name: Seer’s Vision
fixes.reason: "Roll a d20 and record the result. When the target attempts a non-secret saving throw or skill check, they may use the recorded number instead of rolling, ending the spell." The spell was SILENT. It is the fourth spell to leave something waiting for a later check and the FIRST to replace the die rather than modify the roll. Graham ruled on 31 August 2026 that a recorded 20 IS a natural 20 and behaves exactly as though rolled, criticals and open-ended chains included — which is why the implementation forces the FIRST DIE FACE and lets rollChain do the rest, rather than substituting a total and re-deciding three rules it has no business answering. "May use" makes it a prompt, not an automatic application: a recorded 4 is worse than most rolls, and declining keeps the vision because only USING it ends the spell. "Non-secret" is a real distinction here — Appendix 3's Secret trait becomes a blind roll mode, and a player cannot spend a number on a roll they may not see, so a blind check is refused rather than prompted.

fixes.name: Vampiric Touch
fixes.reason: THE DAMAGE WAS IN A PRINTED NOTE AND THE SPELL ROLLED NOTHING. Graham, 1 September 2026: "Vampiric Touch inflicts 6d6 points of essence damage (again look at the rulebook)." The rulebook entry reads "You inflict 6d6 points of essence damage upon the target" behind its Basic Fortitude line, and the pack carried that sentence as a note effect while system.damage.formula was empty — so the Basic save had nothing to halve and the spell did no damage at all. I had reported this as "damage stranded in baseDamage", which was a misreading of what baseDamage is for: it is the per-die base that Empower Spell and the warping options multiply, not the spell's damage. With a formula present the existing basic-save ladder does the rest. THE TEMPORARY HP STAYS A NOTE: "half the damage the target takes" is dynamic and the tempHP effect kind rolls a formula, so it cannot express it yet.

from.text: 6d6 essence (Basic Fortitude); you gain temporary HP equal to half the damage the target takes, lost after 1 minute.

to.text: You gain temporary HP equal to half the damage the target takes, lost after 1 minute — apply by hand; the tempHP effect rolls a formula and cannot yet read the damage actually dealt.

fixes.reason: THE NOTE MUST NOT RESTATE DAMAGE THE SPELL NOW ROLLS. With system.damage carrying 6d6 the card prints the real, halved-or-doubled number, and a note beside it still saying "6d6 essence (Basic Fortitude)" would be two places stating one thing — the defect that produced Ember Of Devotion's "10-ft aura" over a 20 ft template on 31 August. What is left is only the half the system does not do, and it says so.

I reported this one as needing its printed text read before anything could be written; Graham supplied that text on 1 September 2026 and it is unambiguous: "All creatures in the spells area of effect take 20d8 Soul Drain." Typed essence because Soul Drain is the flavour of the Soul trait the spell already carries and essence is the type its sibling Soul spells use (Vampiric Touch, and 16 others in the pack); the pack has no separate soul damage type. The Basic Fortitude line was already present, so the ladder halves and doubles this correctly the moment a formula exists.

fixes.name: Spike Stones

to.text: The spikes are magically concealed: spotting them ahead of time needs a Search check against your Spell DC. The area is also difficult terrain.

fixes.reason: NEW MECHANISM AT 3.454.0, built after `tools/rulebook.mjs` showed three spells sharing one printed sentence that nothing in the system could express: damage PER SQUARE ENTERED. Graham ruled on 1 September 2026 that only the creature's OWN MOVE ACTION triggers it — Wall Of Thorns is the spell that prints the distinction ("uses a move action to enter") and the ruling reads that as the family's rule, so a teleport into the area is free. The concealment and the difficult terrain stay printed: a Search check against the caster's DC is a GM's call about what a creature knew, and this mechanism only answers what it costs to walk in.

fixes.name: Verdant Retribution

to.text: The area is difficult terrain to your enemies; ground that was already difficult terrain due to plants becomes greater difficult terrain as well as hazardous.

fixes.reason: NEW MECHANISM AT 3.454.0, built after `tools/rulebook.mjs` showed three spells sharing one printed sentence that nothing in the system could express: damage PER SQUARE ENTERED. Graham ruled on 1 September 2026 that only the creature's OWN MOVE ACTION triggers it — Wall Of Thorns is the spell that prints the distinction ("uses a move action to enter") and the ruling reads that as the family's rule, so a teleport into the area is free. Printed: "dealing 2d8 poison damage to an enemy each time it enters an affected area (square)". ENEMIES ONLY, declared rather than assumed — it is the one spell of the three that names a side, and the caster's disposition is recorded on the region at cast time so a caster who leaves the scene does not change who their plants attack. THE BASIC FORTITUDE SAVE IS PRINTED, NOT ROLLED: the damage lands after a move the player has already made, and a save prompt arriving then would come after the thing it is meant to halve. GRAHAM'S SECOND RULING of 1 September 2026 governs the area: the printed "all squares on the ground that contain plants" is unknowable to the system, and he chose to treat the whole 80-foot radius as affected.

fixes.name: Wall Of Thorns

to.text: Each 5-foot section has DB 0, Hardness 5 and 20 HP, is immune to critical hits and precision damage, and gives cover to both sides. A destroyed section can be crossed freely — track section HP by hand.

fixes.reason: NEW MECHANISM AT 3.454.0, built after `tools/rulebook.mjs` showed three spells sharing one printed sentence that nothing in the system could express: damage PER SQUARE ENTERED. Graham ruled on 1 September 2026 that only the creature's OWN MOVE ACTION triggers it — Wall Of Thorns is the spell that prints the distinction ("uses a move action to enter") and the ruling reads that as the family's rule, so a teleport into the area is free. Printed: "any creature that uses a move action to enter one of the wall's spaces suffers 2d8 piercing damage". This is the spell whose wording became the family's rule. THE WALL'S OWN HP IS NOT MODELLED and the note says so: sections with Hardness and HP that can be destroyed individually are an object-damage mechanism, not a terrain one, and the +2 PP warp that raises damage "to creatures crossing a DESTROYED section" cannot mean anything until they exist.

fixes.name: Shatter

to.text: The object sustains 2d10 sonic damage, bypassing Hardness 4 or lower — apply by hand. The spell has no save and no attack roll, so nothing resolves the damage automatically.

fixes.reason: FOUND BY DRIVING 3.452.0, and it is a defect I introduced. I gave Shatter `system.damage.formula: "2d10"` and the live card read only "The spell takes effect. 4 PP spent." — no damage rolled, nothing reported. Damage resolves through exactly two routes: `category: "attack"` rolls a spell attack against the target's DB, and `category: "save"` runs the basic-save ladder. Shatter is `category: "utility"` — the book gives an unattended OBJECT automatic damage — so there was no route and the formula sat inert. The formula stays, because it is what the book prints; what was missing was the card saying the number is not being applied. RETIRED at 3.460.0 in favour of `shatter-note-names-the-tool`, which replaced this wording once measuring showed the "automatic damage route" this note anticipated was the wrong build.

fixes.name: Shatter

to.text: The object sustains 2d10 sonic damage, bypassing Hardness 4 or lower. Apply it with the Universal Modifier's item-damage tool, which subtracts Hardness and has an "ignore hardness" tick for this spell's clause — the target is an unattended OBJECT, so there is no creature for the spell to resolve against.

fixes.reason: SUPERSEDES `shatter-damage-note`, which is RETIRED rather than deleted — the tool's own convention since 3.411.0: "the record STAYS, with its reason and its history intact, and declares which fix took over". My first attempt deleted it, which would have thrown away the reason the pack says what it says. THE NOTE SAID WHAT THE SYSTEM CANNOT DO; NOW IT SAYS WHERE THE JOB IS ALREADY DONE. I twice proposed building an "automatic damage route" for spells whose damage has no save and no attack roll, naming Shatter as the proof it was missing. Measuring the pack settled it: 118 spells carry a damage formula, 87 resolve through a save and 30 through an attack, and the ONLY one with no route is Shatter — the one I created the situation for at 3.452.0. A mechanism for a single spell is the over-building this project keeps refusing, and it would have been the wrong mechanism anyway: Shatter targets "1 unattended object", so applying its 2d10 to a creature would be a different spell. THE MODEL IT ACTUALLY NEEDS ALREADY EXISTS — `applyItemDamage(before, amount, hardness)` in the Universal Modifier subtracts an item's Hardness from a damage amount and carries an "Ignore hardness" checkbox, which is exactly the clause Shatter prints. So the note now names that tool instead of describing a gap.

fixes.name: Quench
fixes.reason: Printed: "Non-magical fires within the area are extinguished and fire creatures take 4d8 damage (basic Fortitude)." The spell carried NO damage at all, and that was the safe state rather than an oversight: this system's area/Basic-save ladder would have burned everyone standing in the mist. UNTYPED, deliberately. The book names no damage type for it — the mist is water and the harm is to things made of fire — and every type this pack knows would be wrong: typing it "fire" would be resisted or ignored by the very creatures it is meant to hurt, and there is no water type.

fixes.name: Quench
fixes.reason: `from: null` because the field is ABSENT rather than empty — `damageScope` is new at 3.460.0 and the template addition does not retroactively appear on documents already in the pack. The tool's own header says so; my first draft declared `""` and was correctly refused. GRAHAM'S RULING, 1 September 2026: a "fire creature" is one IMMUNE TO FIRE. Asked how the system should recognise one — there is no Fire trait on creatures and no "fire" among the twelve creature types — he chose the marker already populated on the creatures the spell is about: Fire Dragon, Scaleborn carries immunities "fire, sleep, paralyzed" with a cold weakness. DECLARED ON THE ENTRY, never parsed from the description: "fire creatures take 4d8" is a fact about this spell, and a parser hunting that sentence in prose would find it in spells that mean something else by it. The test is asked of actorDefences rather than the raw field, so a fire Elemental whose immunity comes from its creature type is caught too.

fixes.name: Quench
fixes.reason: The spell prints "(basic Fortitude)" in the same sentence as the damage, and the pack's defence field was empty — so even with a formula the ladder would have applied the full 4d8 with nothing to halve it. The word is what makes the damage scale by degree; verify-basic-save exists because a Basic save with nothing to scale is the word doing nothing, and this is the mirror of that.

fixes.name: Quench

to.text: Non-magical fires in the area are extinguished. You may also select one enchanted flame, fire-based spell or fire-infused item within the vicinity and attempt to counteract it; on a success against an item it loses its fire properties for 10 minutes, and an artifact automatically resists — use the Counteract check, which the system rolls separately.

fixes.reason: THE HALF THIS MECHANISM DOES NOT TOUCH, said plainly rather than implied. Quench has three clauses and only one of them is damage: extinguishing mundane fire is a fact about the scene, and the counteract is a check the system already has its own workflow for (module/counteract.mjs), aimed at a target this spell's picker does not offer. A card showing only the 4d8 would imply the other two had been handled.

fixes.name: Aura Of Vitality
fixes.reason: GRAHAM'S RULING, 1 September 2026: this is an emanation that follows the caster, and the printed "(B)" is the transcription error. The notation means Burst elsewhere in the pack — Deific Presence spells it out as "40-foot burst (B)", and eight spells carry it — but the spell's own text says "You EMIT a comforting glow" and heals "at the beginning of YOUR turn", both of which describe something carried rather than a template left where it was lit. AND THE WORD IS LOAD-BEARING: `emanationIsLive` tests the area string for "emanation", so with "radius" the spell could never become a live emanation and its per-turn heal would never run at all. Corrected at source rather than by widening that test, because the other seven (B) spells really are bursts.

fixes.name: Aura Of Vitality

to.text: The glow also lights the area. +1 PP: the HP healed increases by 1d8 and the recurring or bleed removed by 1 — warped by hand.

fixes.reason: Printed: "At the beginning of your turn, each ally within the spells radius is healed of 2d8 HP of damage and 1 point of recurring or bleed damage." The effects array was EMPTY, so the spell lit nothing and healed nobody. `on: "caster"` is Graham's ruling of 1 September 2026 and is NEW at 3.461.0: the `perTurn` kind has existed since 3.435.1 but `applyPerTurnEmanations` computed its effect with `luminanceTurnEffect`, which reads Luminance's Sustain state and ignores the row entirely — so the `formula` and `mode` fields the pack already carried were read by nothing, and a second spell declaring `perTurn` would have inherited Luminance's growing dice and its undead inversion. THE SIDE IS ALREADY RIGHT: `areaTargeting` is "allies", so "each ally" is the entry's own word rather than an assumption. The warp stays a printed note because raising both the dice and the bleed removed is two numbers, and nothing reads a warp into a per-turn row yet.

fixes.name: Consecrate

to.text: Undead inside also suffer -2 circumstance to all actions and DCs, and no undead can be animated or created within the area. +4 PP: bonuses/penalties +/-1 and the essence damage +1d4 — warped by hand.

fixes.reason: Printed: "all attacks made against undead creatures within the consecrated area gain a +2-circumstance bonus and inflict 1d4 essence secondary damage." The 1d4 was carried nowhere, so the pack could not roll it. Graham ruled on 2 September 2026 that the system applies it rather than printing it for the table: the area is a placed Region and isUndead already exists, so both halves of the sentence are answerable. See module/magic/area-rider.mjs.

fixes.name: Desecrate

to.text: Living creatures inside also suffer -2 circumstance to all actions and DCs, and Spellcraft checks to cast animate undead or create undead gain +2 status inside. +4 PP: bonuses/penalties +/-1 and the essence damage +1d4 — warped by hand.

fixes.reason: Desecrate is Consecrate's sentence with "living" for "undead" — same 1d4 essence secondary damage, carried nowhere. Same mechanism, same ruling.

fixes.name: Force Punch

to.label: Force Punch
to.scope: unarmed

to.text: On a critical hit against a medium or smaller creature the target makes a Will save or is pushed back 5 feet — apply by hand. +4 PP: your unarmed attacks gain a range of 30 feet.

fixes.reason: Printed: "your unarmed attacks inflict 1d6 secondary force damage." The book's own word "secondary" — the strikeRider mechanism exactly, needing only an `unarmed` scope so it rides every unarmed attack rather than one weapon item. `once: false` because the spell lasts a minute and rides every unarmed attack in it, not just the next one.
