fixes.reason: DRIVING IT CAUGHT THIS. The 3.465.0 row omitted `target`, so the applier hung the rider on whatever token happened to be targeted — live, the Wizard cast it and the card read "ZZ Undead Foe: +1d6 force on every unarmed Strike". Force Punch infuses YOUR OWN hand ("You infuse your hand with telekinetic force"), and every other strikeRider row in the pack — Flaming Weapon, Talon Strike, Arrow Of The Wild Hunt — already declares target: self. Mine was the only one that did not.

fixes.name: War Cry
fixes.reason: Printed: "The weapon used to make the Strike deals an additional 1d6 sonic damage and the ally can immediately attempt an additional attack against the same target as a free action." The 1d6 was carried nowhere. Graham ruled on 2 September 2026 that the die lands on the strike that TRIGGERED it (not on the ally's next one) and that the free attack is OFFERED rather than taken. `weapon: melee` is the printed trigger's own word — "a critical strike with a melee weapon". `target: targets` because the printed Targets line is "the triggering ally"; the creature that takes the damage is read from that ally's lastCriticalInjury record. See module/magic/triggered-strike.mjs.

fixes.name: Vital Beacon
fixes.reason: Printed: "It initially restores 4d12 HP but after each use of healing, the die type is reduced by one step. After healing 4d4, the spell ends." None of that was in the pack. Nothing in this system wears out this way — Luminance grows, a charged item counts uses of a fixed thing — so it needed magic/vital-beacon.mjs. Note "AFTER healing 4d4": the 4d4 is rolled and applied and the spell ends afterwards, so there are FIVE uses. The +4 PP bleed option is a separate declared field; the +2 PP extra die is the ordinary warping adder.

fixes.name: Life Siphon
fixes.reason: Printed: "Trigger You cast an arcane soul spell of at least 2 PP ... regaining 1d6 HP per 2 PP of the spell." The dice were carried nowhere. Same shape as War Cry — a reaction to something already done — so it reads a record rather than the board. registerActiveSpell already carries pp/name/castRound but is written only for locked, sustained or live-emanation spells, and an ordinary arcane soul spell registers nothing; hence the new lastCast record. The PP counted is what was SPENT, not the printed cost: a Heroic success halves the total, and "the spell's power" is the power that actually left the caster.

fixes.name: Vital Beacon
fixes.reason: THE PRINTED NUMBERS BELONG IN THE PACK. The first row kept the ladder in code alone, and verify-printed-damage correctly went on reporting Vital Beacon as a spell printing damage the pack cannot roll — the ratchet reads pack rows, and it was right. The steps are now declared where every other spell's dice live; BEACON_STEPS in the module is only the fallback.

fixes.name: Life Siphon
fixes.reason: Same correction as Vital Beacon's ladder: the printed die belongs in the pack. The row said `die: "d6"`, which carries no rollable formula, so verify-printed-damage went on reporting Life Siphon as printing damage the pack cannot roll — correctly. "1d6" is what the book prints, and the formula builder multiplies the COUNT by the number of whole PP pairs.

fixes.name: Flame Prison

to.label: Flame Prison
notes: The bars inflict 1d6 fire damage per minute in the cage, and 2d6 for touching them — apply by hand.
If the cage takes more than 150 points of water or cold damage it is destroyed.

fixes.reason: Printed: an escape ladder of 8d6 / 16d6 / 24d6 / 24d6 fire, with a Minor Fire critical on Failure and a Serious one on Fumble — and only Fumble keeps you in. None of it was in the pack, including the 24d6. The ladder runs the WRONG WAY for this system (better roll, less damage) and is four printed numbers rather than one scaled by degree, so it is stored as four. Graham ruled on 2 September 2026: the attempt is a button, the prisoner is marked, and the per-minute die and the bars are printed rather than rolled — a minute is ten rounds and nothing in this system ticks on it.

fixes.name: Force Prison

to.label: Force Prison
notes: The prison is immune to damage. Objects, attacks and effects may not pass through, except aligned damage, electricity damage and sonic attacks.
The caster chooses whether air enters; if not, the prisoner is in suspended animation and needs no air, food or drink.

fixes.reason: Force Prison is Flame Prison's sentence with different numbers — 8d6 / 12d6 / 16d6 / 16d6 force. Note the ladders are NOT the same shape: Flame doubles from Critical to Success and Force does not, and that is why the four degrees are stored rather than derived from one number.

fixes.name: Elemental Shield
fixes.reason: Printed: "any adjacent creature that attacks you with a melee attack must make a Basic Reflex saving throw or take 2d6 damage", plus resistance to the element OPPOSITE the one chosen. The 2d6 was carried nowhere. The rider is the `thorns` mechanism Vibrant Thorns already proved, given a printed save (the position hazard-terrain took for Verdant Retribution: this fires inside somebody else's completed Strike, and a prompt would arrive after the damage it is meant to halve). Graham ruled on 2 September 2026 that resistance halves and has no value, which damage.mjs already implements — so the effect grants a resistance TYPE. `Base Damage 1d6` on the entry is the Empower multiplier and is NOT the damage; that misreading was corrected on 1 September 2026.

fixes.name: Nexus Of Elemental Energy

to.label: Nexus Of Elemental Energy
notes: Spells with the chosen elemental trait cast against creatures in the area increase their total damage by one die and apply a -2 circumstance penalty to saves made to resist them — apply by hand.

fixes.reason: Printed: a five-degree save ladder for anyone beginning a turn in the zone — Critical unaffected, Success 2d6, Partial 4d6, Failure 4d6 plus a Minor Critical, Fumble 4d6 plus a Light Critical. None of it was in the pack. The zone is a PLACE ("Area 10-foot radius, Range 60 feet"), so it is a Region and not an emanation; the element is chosen at cast and decides the SAVE (Fortitude for acid and cold, Reflex for electricity and fire), using the table that shipped with Elemental Shield at 3.473.0. Graham ruled on 2 September 2026 that a "Light Critical" reads as SERIOUS — the book's own table defines only Minor, Serious and Deadly, and a Fumble must be worse than the Failure line's Minor. He also ruled the clause about elemental spells cast into the zone is printed rather than applied: it reaches into every other spell's damage and save DC from outside.

fixes.name: Missile Storm
fixes.reason: Printed: "Each target is hit by 2d6 +6 magic missiles (each inflicting 1d4+1 force damage) + 1d6 additional missiles per Size category above Medium." None of those numbers were carried anywhere, so a 20 PP spell resolved as a utility with no damage at all. The count is itself rolled, which nothing else in this pack does, so it is stored as its four parts rather than as one formula. Graham ruled on 3 September 2026 that the salvo lands automatically (there is no save line and the sentence is "is hit by") and that the size clause counts the TARGET's size, so each creature caught rolls its own count.

fixes.name: Missile Storm
fixes.reason: Printed: "YOU MAY TARGET each character in the spells area of effect." Graham's ruling of 3 September 2026, after driving 3.478.0 showed the caster caught in his own 50-foot radius and reduced to 0 HP by his own spell: "The spell targets characters in the area of effect 'You may target...'. So the caster would choose who was affected within the area and who was not." Missile Storm is the ONLY area spell in the pack whose text prints a choice of targets - every other area is swept, so the field is opt-in rather than a blanket picker over every area spell.

fixes.name: Orb Of Acid
fixes.reason: Printed: "you deal 1d6 acid damage plus 1 splash acid damage", and "CL 4+: the damage increases by 1d6 and the splash damage by 1". REPORTED BY GRAHAM FROM A LIVE SESSION, 2 September 2026: the spell reported no splash damage. The entry carried effects: [] so the splash was prose read by nothing. perStep 1 rides the same caster-level steps the dice ladder already uses.

fixes.name: Acid Bolt
fixes.reason: Printed: "you deal 4d6 acid damage plus 2 splash acid damage". The second of the pack's only two splash spells, found by the same sweep as Orb Of Acid. Its persistent-on-critical clause is NOT covered here - that is a separate printed number and stays on the flat-damage backlog rather than being folded in silently.

fixes.name: Daze

from.text: increase the damage by 1d4 and the Save DC increases by 2.

to.text: increase the damage by 1d4 and the Save DC increases by 2.

fixes.reason: Printed: "CL 4+: increase the damage by 1d4 and the Save DC increases by 2." The row carried damageDice: "" - an EMPTY string - so the Save DC climbed every four caster levels and the damage never moved. Daze was the only one of the pack's eleven PP 0 damaging cantrips whose dice did not scale; the other ten all carry a recurring threshold-4 ladder. Found when Graham asked on 3 September 2026 that every damaging cantrip scale the same way.

fixes.name: Orb Of Fire

from.text: The damage increases by 1d6 and the persistent by 1.

to.text: The damage increases by 1d6 and the persistent by 1.

fixes.reason: Printed: "CL 4+: The damage increases by 1d6 AND THE PERSISTENT BY 1." The dice climbed; the persistent did not, because nothing read a caster-level ladder for it - system.damage.persistent was a stored field adjusted only by warping. A 12th-level caster dealt 4d6 and the same 1 recurring as at 1st. applyCasterLevelMods now resolves `persistent` alongside the dice, so any spell whose ladder raises it gets this.

fixes.name: Serenity
fixes.reason: Printed: "Critical The target is unaffected. Success 5 Mental damage. Failure 10 Mental damage and -20 critical injury. Fumble 10 Mental damage and a critical injury." The entry carried effects: [] and damage: {} - a 12 PP spell that did nothing at all. Critical's damage is 0 rather than absent, because "unaffected" is a decided outcome and a missing rung is one nobody decided. GRAHAM'S RULING, 4 September 2026: the save is rolled ONCE and its result is suffered again on every offensive action, so the degree is recorded on the target rather than re-rolled.

fixes.name: Word Of Death
fixes.reason: Printed: "Critical 20 damage. Success 50 damage; if this brings the target to 0 HP, the target dies instantly. Failure If the target has 100 HP or fewer, it dies instantly; otherwise it drops to -10 HP. Fumble The target dies instantly." Carried nowhere - a 20 PP spell that did nothing. The ladder runs the WRONG WAY as the prisons do (Success 50 is worse than Critical 20), so it is four printed outcomes rather than one derived rule. immuneSeconds 600 is "once targeted, the target is then temporarily immune for 10 minutes", carried by the existing temporary-immunity mechanism.

fixes.name: Reaper’s Resonance

from.text: Trigger — a creature within 20 ft dies: heal HP equal to its level + 5 (doubled if it was undead).

fixes.reason: Printed: "A creature within 20 feet of you dies or is destroyed... healing HP equal to the level of the triggering creature plus 5. If the triggering creature was undead, the amount healed is doubled." The note was a reminder and nothing read it. castAP is Reaction, so the caster casting it IS the trigger (Graham's ruling of 28 Aug 2026 for reaction spells) - there is no hook to write. The arithmetic, the doubling and the +2 PP bleed warp are in magic/death-resonance.mjs.

fixes.name: Bless Water
fixes.reason: Printed: "You imbue a flask of water with positive energy, turning it into holy water." Cost: religious ingredients worth 15 gp. Carried effects: [] - the spell did nothing at all. Holy Water is a REAL alchemical pack entry (consumable, 25 gp, traits Alchemical Bomb Consumable Essence Good Splash), so the spell copies that document rather than fabricating one: a hand-built imitation would have lacked the Splash trait the 3.482.0 splash mechanism reads, and the reagent clause. The 15 gp is printed rather than deducted - no spell component cost is charged anywhere in this system.

fixes.name: Fools Riches

to.text: Printed: on a Success the creature is fixated "until it completes its first action on its next turn"; automated as 2 rounds so the penalty lands on that action rather than expiring before the creature acts. On a Critical the creature disbelieves the illusion and is unaffected. A creature that enters the 5-foot area recognises the illusion and is not at risk.

fixes.reason: Printed: Will save, 5-foot burst, "Any creature within 20 feet of the area ... must make a Will saving throw", sustained up to 1 minute. Carried effects: [] - the spell did nothing. THREE DECISIONS. (1) CONDITION: the book says "fascinated"; there is no Fascinated condition in this system and Graham ruled on 4 September 2026 that Fascinated should be Fixated - the same ruling applied to critical row 87-88. (2) SAVE NET: the area is a 5-foot burst but the save net is 20 feet, so the template alone would have caught only creatures standing in the single square the spell says are IMMUNE. Graham ruled 20 feet from the CENTRE, not 20 from the burst's edge (25). Declared as catchRadiusFeet and read by declaredSaveNetFeet; the card names the wider net because the drawn shape and the caught list otherwise contradict each other. (3) SUCCESS DURATION: "until it completes its first action on its next turn" parses to null and occurs once in the whole book. 1 round would expire before the creature acts, making the entire rung a silent no-op; 2 rounds lands the fixation on that first action and overstates only by later actions in the same turn. The printed wording is carried on the card as a qualitative remainder rather than discarded. Only critical/success/failure are declared, so effectiveSaveDegree maps heroic->critical and partial/fumble/blunder->failure, matching the printed three-rung ladder.

fixes.name: Umbral Veil
fixes.reason: Printed: "Within a 20-foot emanation centred on the target, the illumination level is reduced by three steps (to a minimum of 2)." Carried effects: [] - the spell did nothing. NOT the `light` effect kind: that grants a light SOURCE from a registry of torches and lanterns with printed radii, and Umbral Veil emits nothing - it changes what the illumination level IS inside a circle, so a torch carried into the shadow is still three steps dimmer than it would be outside it. The shift is read after light sources for exactly that reason. `follows: true` anchors the emanation to the TARGET rather than the caster, which is new at 3.490.0 - the spell is cast at touch on "1 willing creature" and the circle is theirs. `droppable: true` is Graham's ruling of 4 September 2026 (build the drop, print the retrieval): 1 AP Interact sets the anchor to null, the circle stays where it was let go and keeps dimming for the remaining duration, and "if someone retrieves the cloak the spell abruptly ends" is printed on the card for the GM to end from the Spellcasting panel. Steps, floor, radius and follows are all declared per spell because Unwelcome Halo (PP 2, +2 steps, degree-gated duration) and Darkness (PP 4, -4 steps, min 3, static, warps that move both numbers) disagree with this spell on every one of them; neither is wired here, because they are not PP 1.

fixes.name: Silent Binding

to.label: Silent Binding
to.text: Its whispers are muffled, making them inaudible to creatures more than 10 feet away without a successful Perception check. This also interferes with auditory and linguistic effects, as well as communication. The target can still speak and perform verbal spell components.

to.label: Silent Binding
to.text: Its whispers are muffled, making them inaudible to creatures more than 10 feet away without a successful Perception check. This also interferes with auditory and linguistic effects, as well as communication. The target can still speak and perform verbal spell components.

to.label: Silent Binding
to.text: Its whispers are muffled, making them inaudible to creatures more than 10 feet away without a successful Perception check. This also interferes with auditory and linguistic effects, as well as communication. The target can still speak and perform verbal spell components.

fixes.reason: Printed: Fortitude save, 30 feet, 1 creature, duration varies. "Its whispers are muffled, making them inaudible to creatures more than 10 feet away without a successful Perception check against your spell DC." Critical unaffected / Success 1 round / Failure 1 minute / Fumble 10 minutes. Carried effects: [] - the spell did nothing. NOT A CONDITION: there is no Muffled condition; the word appears twice in the whole rulebook (here and an unrelated wild-magic row) and Appendix 2 does not list it, while "auditory" and "linguistic" are TRAITS rather than conditions. Inventing one would put a word on the sheet the book never prints - the argument markers.mjs already made for Stabilise. NOT A MARKER EITHER: a marker exists to be read by a named subsystem and verify-markers refuses one with no reader, and there is no reader to write - both Perception actions in this system, Awareness and Search, are declared against: "none" because the GM sets their difficulty. So what is automated is the NUMBER: the spell DC is computed once at the cast, printed on the card and carried on the target's Effects tab beside a duration that expires by itself, and the adjudication (whether a listener is close enough, what else the effect impedes) is stated on the card as the GM's. Graham approved the mechanism on 4 September 2026 on the measurement rather than the spell: ELEVEN silent spells from PP 1 to PP 16 publish a DC for somebody else's check - Pass Without Trace, Rope Trick, Lock, Disgrace, Resonance Manipulation, Spirit Mark, Tree Shape, Inner Sanctum, Volcanic Inferno, Punishing Winds - differing only in which check and by how much, hence offset (Lock's +5) and atLeast (Pass Without Trace's "whichever option is higher"). Only critical/success/failure/fumble are printed; the critical rung is "unaffected" and correctly carries no row, and effectiveSaveDegree maps heroic->critical, partial->failure and blunder->fumble.

fixes.name: Enchanting Utterance

from.text: Failure or fumble: the target cannot take hostile actions against you for the duration.

to.text: Failure: the target is unable to take hostile actions against you for the duration — GM-adjudicated.
Fumble: the target is also unable to take hostile actions against you for the duration — GM-adjudicated.

fixes.reason: Printed ladder: Critical unaffected / Success -1 circumstance to attack and damage against you / Failure the target is unable to take hostile actions against you / Fumble stunned 1 AND unable to take hostile actions. The pack declared only success and fumble; the FAILURE rung's whole content is GM-adjudicated, so it was written as prose inside an ungated note reading 'Failure or fumble: ...'. That was harmless while an unnamed degree read upward to the milder neighbour, and became wrong the moment Graham's ruling of 4 September 2026 made the failure side read DOWNWARD: with no failure rung declared, a plain Failure fell to the Fumble rung and picked up stunned 1, a condition the book gives only on a Fumble. Fixed by declaring the rung rather than by exempting the spell - notes now honour onSave (backward-compatible: no note in the pack declared one before this release, and an ungated note prints exactly as before), so the Failure clause is a rung of the ladder instead of prose about one. The fumble half of the old sentence becomes its own fumble-gated note so each rung says what it does. Blunder still clamps to fumble, and Critical still applies nothing because an unnamed SAVING degree is how 'the target is unaffected' is represented.

fixes.name: Gravity Weapon

from.text: The weapon's base damage die gains +2 for the duration (warpable to +4, or two weapons).

fixes.reason: Printed: "You empower the kinetic energy and density of one chosen weapon in your grasp. The base damage die of the weapon gains a +2 bonus for duration of the spell." Carried a NOTE and nothing else - automation that was really a reminder. Graham ruled on 4 September 2026 that this is a FLAT +2 to the damage rolled, not a die step: the warp says "increase the DAMAGE by an additional +2 (max +4)", which is a number with a numeric cap; seven weapons in the pack are already d12 and would have nowhere to step, gaining nothing from either the spell or its 4 PP warp; and a step is weaker than the flat bonus (d6+2 averages 5.5, d8 averages 4.5), which is a strange thing to charge 4 PP for. NOT A STRIKE RIDER: a rider is a second typed packet with its own dice (Flaming Weapon's 1d6 fire) and refuses a row with no dice and no damage type, deliberately - strike-riders.mjs was right to record this spell as out of scope. Gravity Weapon adds no packet; it makes the weapon's OWN damage bigger in the weapon's own type, so it is a flat addition to the formula resolveWeaponDamage already assembles, beside The Bigger They Are and Weapon Specialisation. Scoped to the chosen weapon via the same promptRiderWeapon the strike riders use, so "which weapon" is answered one way in this system; unscoped it would arm every weapon the character owns, which is the defect Talon Strike's weaponScoped exists to prevent. The +4 PP cap is enforced in the pure module and again across all live records, so two castings on one blade cannot stack to +8.

fixes.name: Wild Morph
fixes.reason: Printed: "You gain a single natural attack form from one of your Studied Targets." Carried effects: [] - the spell did nothing. THE DESIGN WAS DECIDED BY WHAT A STUDIED TARGET IS. applyStudyOutcome records either {name, type:"creature", id} when a token was studied, or {name, type:"named"} when it was typed - because Study Target's own prompt asks "what did you study - a person, place, or thing?" and a place has no statblock. So the spell cannot simply read a creature's attacks: half its subjects are not creatures, and a creature entry's id may belong to an actor since deleted or to an unlinked token. Graham's ruling of 4 September 2026: pick the Studied Target, name the attack form, and grant a REAL one - a Strikeable weapon item on the sheet, tagged to the cast and removed when the spell ends. Where the creature DOES resolve, its own natural attacks prefill the second prompt, which is still the ruling (the player names the form) and merely stops them retyping what the system can already read. The item is modelled on the Hybrid Bite that Hybrid Transformation grants, category Unarmed included - without it a grown claw would be the only natural attack in the game carrying a -4, because the proficiency engine reads the category. Cleanup is new at this release: expireSpellEffects and removeEffectsByCastId both now delete items stamped endsWithSpell, so a form cannot survive one ending and not the other, while Bless Water's Holy Water - also created by a spell, and meant to be kept - is untouched because it does not declare it. THE TWO "INSTEAD" WARPS ARE PRINTED, NOT BUILT: a movement type and a special ability from a Studied Target replace the attack with things this system has no general shape for, so the card names them as the GM's. The +2 PP "additional attack form (max 3)" IS built, because only the count changes.

The other two warps keep mods: {} DELIBERATELY and are not inert by oversight: they replace the attack form with a movement type or a special ability, neither of which this system has a general shape for, and wildMorphRemainderLine names both on every cast as the GM's to adjudicate. fixes.name: Delayed Respite
fixes.reason: Printed: Reaction, trigger "a creature or object within range takes damage from an attack", 30 feet, duration 1 round (D). "Although damage and critical hits are determined as usual, the target's HP remain unaffected, and no other effects of the attack take hold until the spell's duration has passed. Once the spell ends, the results of the attack manifest instantly." Carried effects: [] - the spell did nothing. SCOPED ON 29 AUGUST AND RULED ON 4 SEPTEMBER. The damage half is ONE gate: all sixteen damage routes cross applyDamageAndCheckDying, and the 3.339.4 permission relay is the precedent for intercepting exactly there. "No other effects take hold" is NOT: conditions are a separate path with twelve call sites and critical injuries are rolled inline in the attack workflow, so deferring only the damage would leave the critical landing anyway and the table concluding the spell worked. Graham ruled: defer the damage, print the rest - the card names the critical, the conditions and the bleed on every cast as the GM's to hold alongside it. THE FOUR SUB-RULINGS: dismissal FIRES the stored packet immediately ("once the spell ends, the results manifest instantly" - dismissal is an ending, which makes it a weapon rather than a mercy); the packet still lands if the target dies of something else first (a delay, not an escape); healing during the round does NOT reduce the packet, it raises the hit points the packet then eats into ("the results manifest in full", which is what makes it a delay rather than a negation); and ONE ATTACK, ONE PACKET - "the triggering creature" and "the impact of the attack" both read singular, so a Respite that has caught a blow catches no more and a second blow in the same round lands now. Both endings - the world clock and dismissal - release through one function so they cannot disagree, and the packet is cleared before it is applied so a double release cannot deal it twice.

fixes.name: Spell Storing
fixes.reason: Printed: PP 1, touch, until next daily preparation. "The next spell that you cast within one round is stored in your Mage Staff. The stored Spell has no immediate effect (other than of being stored), but you can then release the spell at any time for 1 AP. You may only have one spell stored in your staff at any one time and if you cast the spell again the last spell you stored is dismissed." Carried effects: [] - the spell did nothing, and both warps carried mods: {} and bought nothing. GRAHAM'S RULINGS, 4 and 5 September 2026. (1) PP AT STORAGE, EVERYTHING ELSE AT RELEASE: "the next spell that you CAST" pays at storage; what is suspended is the effect, not the payment, and "has no immediate effect" means nothing was resolved then - a degree rolled at storage would be fixed before any target existed, and saves cannot be rolled until release anyway. (2) THE COLLISION THAT RULING COULD NOT ANTICIPATE, found by measuring castingOutcome before building: THE PRICE DEPENDS ON THE DEGREE (heroic half total, critical half base plus warp, success total, PARTIAL ZERO, failure half, fumble and blunder total), so "pay at storage" cannot know what to charge. Ruled 5 September: CHARGE THE FULL SUCCESS PRICE AT STORAGE AND SETTLE AT RELEASE, so every degree costs exactly what the book says - a Heroic hands half back, a Partial hands it all back, a Fumble keeps what it took. The alternative, charging full and keeping it, would have made storing quietly more expensive than casting. (3) "YOUR MAGE STAFF" IS THE ARCANE BOND: nothing else in the pack mentions a Mage Staff (0 of 692 spells besides this one, 0 items, 0 abilities), and Arcane Bond's "designate a single item you own" is a wizard's staff in everything but name - so the store lives on the designated item and a wizard who has not designated one today cannot store. The intercept is ONE GATE at the top of castSpell, the same reasoning as Delayed Respite's damage gate: every cast route crosses that function.

fixes.name: Spirit Of The Hunt

from.text: Advantage on Search (Perception) checks for the duration.

fixes.reason: Printed: PP 1, 1 living target, 10 minutes. "A spirit animal blesses the targets senses granting advantage on Search (Perception) checks for the duration." +2 PP: also gain advantage on Track (Survival) checks. +2 PP: target an additional creature. It shipped as a NOTE - automation that is really a reminder - and both warps carried mods: {}. Both `search` and `track` exist as action keys in data/skill-actions.mjs, so the scope is exactly the printed one rather than the whole Perception or Survival skill, and both entries are `auto` because the action a check was invoked from settles the scope with no judgement needed. The Track warp is wired through the generic extraConditionals count. THE SECOND WARP IS STILL PRINTED: 46 warps across the pack sell an additional target and none is wired, because nothing in the system parses or enforces a spell's printed target count at all - the picker offers everyone and the player ticks whom they like. Graham ruled on 5 September that the target cap is its own release, next. The conditional machinery in module/conditionals.mjs already holds this exact rule - "a bonus that is PERMANENT but SCOPED" - with eight scope axes and a collector that reads BOTH items and actor.appliedEffects. That second home is what lets a spell grant one, so nothing new was invented: the spell effect carries flags[trg-prime].conditionals and every check picks it up. Graham's direction, 5 September 2026: build Spirit Of The Hunt as a scoped advantage conditional, which unblocks Cancel Magic, Courage and Flawless Lies with it.

Found on 5 September 2026 while wiring Spirit Of The Hunt's second warp; Graham ruled the cap should be built as its own release. `extraTargets` is a generic COUNT and an INCREMENT, so a warp taken twice buys two. The cap is enforced in cast-workflow.mjs after the warp chooser and before the Spellcraft check, so a refusal costs nothing, and it REFUSES rather than trimming: taking "the first N" would apply the spell to creatures the player did not choose. This spell's warp: "per additional target". NARROWED AT 3.519.0: this fix declared the whole array as its from/to while editing one warp's `mods`, so it began refusing whenever a SIBLING warp changed. It now names the field it sets. See _why.

fixes.name: Sacrificing Shield
fixes.reason: Printed: PP 1, Reaction, 30 feet, Warding. "You shield your ally by absorbing their wounds. The HP damage that would have been inflicted upon them is reduced by 5. However, you absorb this damage instead, and any immunities, weaknesses, or resistances you possess do not come into effect. Be aware that you only absorb HP damage with this spell and suffer no effects from any other part of the attack." Carried effects: [], duration "", targets "" - the spell did nothing. THE GATE IS THE LINE DELAYED RESPITE ALREADY USES: the number reaching applyDamageDirect has crossed the target's resistances upstream in resolveAgainstDefences, so a redirect placed there gets "only HP damage" and "your resistances do not apply" without implementing either. GRAHAM RULED, 5 September 2026, on the three things the printed entry does not say. (1) THE WINDOW: a Reaction with no printed duration, and Foundry cannot let a reaction interrupt a blow already being applied - so the ward is cast in anticipation and lasts ONE ROUND, exactly as Delayed Respite does, spent by the first blow it reduces. An untimed ward would have let a caster pre-cast at leisure every morning, which is what a reaction cost exists to prevent. (2) THE CASTER'S STATE: dying, unconscious and beyond the printed 30 feet all still absorb - the spell was paid for at casting and an ally has been counting on it since. ONLY A DELETED CASTER stops the redirect, and the card says so. (3) THE +2 PP CONDITION WARP IS NOT BUILT: applyConditionTags has 28 call sites across 11 files and its own comment records that most of the forty or so places that apply conditions never call it, so there is no single primitive to hang an absorb on. Building it against the helper alone would work on some routes and fail invisibly on the rest. The warp stays purchasable and the card prints the clause for the GM to move by hand - the same answer Delayed Respite's "no other effects of the attack take hold" got. The redirect sits BELOW temporary HP (damage a temporary pool swallowed inflicted no HP damage, so a ward above the pool would be spent on a blow the ally shrugged off) and ABOVE the dying machinery (the caster's points are meant to be the ones the ally does not take).

fixes.name: Sacrificing Shield

Graham ruled one round on 5 September 2026, matching Delayed Respite - the only other Reaction ward in the pack - so the two spells that both wait for an incoming blow wait for the same length of time. The (D) makes it dismissible, which 3.494.0 taught the system to register and honour.

fixes.name: Sacrificing Shield
fixes.reason: THE INERT-WARP DEFECT, HIDING IN THE CODE RATHER THAN THE DATA. Found live on 5 September 2026 during the 3.499.0 test pass: the warp was bought, the cast card printed "Warped - +2 PP: you may also absorb any condition that the target suffers", and the remainder line went on telling the table that conditions were nobody's to move. The reader was `warpMods.applied.some(w => /condition/i.test(w.text))` - matching the CHOSEN WARP'S TEXT rather than a declared mod - and `applied` is not a key on what arrives at applySpellEffects: aggregateWarpSelection returns {ppSpent, rawPP, mods, notes} and only `mods` is passed on, so the test was permanently false. Text-matching a warp was a shortcut around exactly this data fix, and it failed for a reason no better regular expression would have fixed. `absorbConditions` is a FLAG rather than a count, the shape storedReleaseReaction and freezeMembership take: the clause names no quantity, so taking it twice buys the same thing. THE WARP ITSELF STAYS DEFERRED - applyConditionTags has 28 call sites across 11 files and there is no single primitive to hang an absorb on - so what this mod buys is the printed clause telling the GM to move the conditions by hand. fixes.name: Verdant Snare
fixes.reason: Printed: PP 1, 1 AP, 30 feet, 10-ft radius, Alteration. "Roots and vines lash out, creating natural difficult terrain until the start of your next turn." Carried effects: [] - the spell did nothing at all. THE BEHAVIOUR ALREADY EXISTED: creature-aura-workflow.mjs has built Foundry `modifyMovementCost` behaviours since the creature auras went in, complete with the schema-guard note recording what happened when an unknown key was silently dropped and every difficulty defaulted to 1. The `difficultTerrain` kind hands that same builder an aura-shaped descriptor rather than being right about the schema twice, and it is the SEVENTH region-claiming kind - added only once 3.500.0 gave a claimed Region an ending, because before that a patch of vines would have outlived the session it was cast in. DOUBLE IS THE MULTIPLIER and it is the system's own word: "difficult terrain, in this system, costs double" (combat/fly.mjs). Not an illusion, so no disbelief clause is printed - a card that recites every clause a spell might have had is one nobody reads by the third cast. Its two warps were already live: +2 PP declares areaGrowth/areaMax and +3 PP declares durationText.

Graham ruled 1 round on 5 September 2026: the system stamps rounds already, and in initiative a round from now IS the start of your next turn. Slightly generous when cast mid-turn, and consistent with every other round-stamped spell rather than introducing a duration shape that ends on a specific creature's turn - a shape nothing else in the system uses. It matters twice over now: 3.500.0 expires the spell's Region on that stamp, so with an empty field the vines would have been permanent, and the +3 PP warp that buys "1 minute" would have been the only version with a clock at all. THE REFERENCE STILL RECORDS WHAT WAS PRINTED.

fixes.name: Warped Terrain
fixes.reason: Printed: PP 1, 1 AP+, 60 feet, "5-foot radius or more", 1 minute, Shadow/Visual. "You conjure illusory hazards that cover the ground ... causing any creature that traverses them to perceive the area as difficult terrain. However, a creature can attempt to disbelieve the illusion by using a Search action ... If successful, the creature sees through the deception and can move through the area unaffected for the remaining duration." Carried effects: [] - the spell did nothing. `illusory: true` is what makes the Region name and the cast card carry the disbelief clause. GRAHAM RULED 5 September 2026 that disbelief is NAMED, NOT AUTOMATED: Foundry's movement-cost behaviour is a property of the REGION and charges everyone inside, with no per-token exemption - the identical limit terrainBehaviours already records for a creature aura's `exemptTrait`. The two alternatives were worse: tracking who has disbelieved would record the fact and still charge them, which is a list that lies; and suppressing the Region once anyone sees through it would free the whole battlefield because one creature made a Search check.

fixes.reason: "1 AP+" HAD NO HOME. "By investing additional actions while casting the spell, you can expand the radius of the illusion. Each extra AP spent increases the radius by 5 feet, allowing you to extend the deceptive terrain up to a maximum of 10 extra feet when utilizing 3 AP." Measured before building: of 692 spells, exactly ONE carries a castAP with a "+" - this one - so the shape is deliberately small and spell-agnostic rather than a general action-economy feature built from a sample of one. IT IS NOT `apOptions`: all fourteen spells carrying that field use it as a VARIANT CHOOSER (Shape Of The Wyrm's six forms, Iron Body's single alternative), each a complete {ap, label, range, area, effects} replacing the cast, and squeezing "+5 feet per AP" in would mean three near-identical clones of one spell whose only difference is a radius. IT IS NOT A WARP EITHER, though it is offered beside them: a warp is bought with PP and raises the Casting DC, and this is bought with ACTIONS and does not - folding it in would have raised the DC for spending an action, which the book never says. What it shares with a warp is where it lands: `areaGrowth` is the mod warp-area.mjs already reads.

fixes.name: Hide From Animals
fixes.reason: Printed: PP 1, 2 AP, touch, 1 creature, 1 minute, Shadow. "Animals cannot sense the warded creature. Even extraordinary or supernatural sensory capabilities, such as blindsense, blindsight, scent, and tremorsense, cannot detect or locate warded creatures. Animals simply act as though the warded creature is not there. If a warded character touches an animal or attacks any creature, even with a spell, the spell ends." Carried effects: [] - the spell did nothing. Its one warp was already live (`extraTargets`). GRAHAM RULED, 5 September 2026: AUTOMATE THE ENDING, NARRATE THE HIDING. There is no perception or detection machinery in this system for "animals cannot sense you" to hook into, and building one would be a far larger release than the spell that asked for it - so the GM runs that half and BOTH the effect's own name and the cast card say so. THE ENDING IS THE HALF A TABLE FORGETS: a ward that should have ended three rounds ago is not a dispute anybody notices, it is a player quietly still hidden with no reason to check. It ends at two gates this system already owns as single choke points - `rollWeaponAttack` and `castSpell` - which is the argument Delayed Respite's damage gate made and Sacrificing Shield's inherited; a ward that asked each caller to remember would end on a Strike from the sheet and not on one from a reaction feat. "EVEN WITH A SPELL" INCLUDES A SPELL THAT MAKES NO ATTACK ROLL: `castEndsHiding` counts a spell that is an attack OR declares a defence, reading the same two fields `spellHasNoMechanics` uses rather than inventing a third opinion about what hostile means. The error is pointed deliberately: over-ending costs a player a minute of a 1 PP spell, while under-ending leaves them hidden from things that can see them, which is the failure nobody notices until it has decided a fight. NOT BUILT AS A GENERAL ENDS-ON-ATTACK SHAPE, and that was measured: three other spells print a sentence about ending near the word attack and none is this shape - Mirage Entity and Project Image end when the image IS HIT, the opposite direction, and Delayed Respite's mention is about the blow it holds. A sample of one, so it is named for what it does, the same conclusion ap-scale.mjs reached for "1 AP+".

fixes.name: Self Mirage

to.label: Self Mirage
to.scope: see through your disguise

fixes.reason: SELF MIRAGE WAS INERT TWICE OVER, and this is Grahams ruling of 6 Sep 2026: "Any modifiers to Disguise should benefit the disguised character so the DC required to pierce the disguise should be increased."  FIRST, it was scoped to the `disguise` action - one of only TWO of the 97 declared skill actions carrying `checkType: none`. `checkConfiguration` returns null for those, so no check object is built and no actionKey ever reaches `matchesCheck`. The bonus was attached to a roll that does not happen.  SECOND, it was on the wrong side of the roll anyway. The printed +4 covers "Deception checks to prevent others from seeing through your disguise", and the disguised character makes no such check: Pierce Disguise is the OBSERVERS Sense Motive roll, declared `against: skillDC:deception`, so the number that matters is a DC on the defenders own sheet.  This is the same shape as the Storgar shove bonus that `module/combat/defence-dc.mjs` was built for on Grahams ruling of 16 Aug 2026 - "there is no such check, so the bonus belongs on the DC side" - so it goes through that channel, which gained skill DCs at 3.506.0 to carry it.  A `deception` SLOT bonus was the alternative and was refused: it would also have raised every Bluff, Feint and Create a Diversion the caster makes for the duration, which the book does not grant.  DECLARED AS A SECOND FIX RATHER THAN FOLDED INTO THE FIRST, because the conditional row genuinely shipped in 3.504.0 - the chain [] -> conditional -> DC bonus is what happened, and it replays onto a fresh pack in that order.  ITS `from` IS THE FRESH-PACK STATE, not the intermediate one: the superseded fix above is skipped rather than applied, so on a clean pack this is what moves `[]` to the DC bonus in one step, and on a pack that already holds it the tool reports it done.

fixes.name: Magic Stone
fixes.reason: MAGIC STONE SHIPPED WITH `effects: []` - one of the four PP 2 spells deliberately left unbuilt in the 3.504.0 batch, and the last of them that could be built without a new rule.  ALMOST EVERYTHING IT NEEDS ALREADY EXISTED. The pebbles are a real piece of AMMUNITION: `ammunitionFitsWeapon` matches a round to a weapon by GROUP and the Slings group is "Sling"; `roundsRemaining` and the consume step spend one per shot, which is "crumbles to dust after it is used" with nothing added; and the attack workflow already folds a rounds damage modifier into the formula.  WHAT DID NOT EXIST WAS HALF THE BONUS. Ammunition could change damage, damage type, range, armour rending, splash and subdual - everything except whether the shot lands. Grahams ruling of 7 September 2026 is that "+1 item (magic) bonus" covers ATTACK AND DAMAGE, so `attackModifier` was added to the ammunition template in the same release. All nine authored rounds declare zero and are unaffected.  `target: self` MATCHES HEALING EARTH, which is the closer analogue than Bless Water: both name an OBJECT as the target ("up to 3 pebbles", "a handful of dirt or mud") and the caster is who ends up carrying the result. The player hands them on through the inventory like any other item.  THE DISRUPTIVE TRAIT IS PRINTED, NOT APPLIED. Measured before building: "Disruptive" appears in NO pack and in NO line of code anywhere in this system, and "Magical" exists on three documents that nothing reads. There is no rule for the pebbles to carry, so the trait goes on the item where a reader sees it and the card says the table settles it.

"A creature may only benefit from one restoration spell each day" limits the BENEFICIARY and names ONE spell; a shared boolean would have let a Restoration block some future relief spell on the same creature. GRAHAMS RULING, 7 September 2026: track it on the target, cleared by THEIR daily preparations - a cleric who rests while the patient does not has not renewed the patients day.  A CHANNEL, NOT A SPELL: seven warps across THREE spells redirect a condition reduction - Restoration (four), Animal Healing (two) and Renewals Touch (two, though its reductions are per-turn options the TARGET chooses rather than something the cast does, so they do not ride this).  EVERY CONDITION IT NAMES ALREADY EXISTED and every one is VALUED - fatigued, dazed, weakened, injured, doomed and soulDrain are all in the registry with steps to come down. That is why this spell was chosen: the vocabulary was there and only the sentence was missing.

ONE PURCHASE OFFERING TWO, which is why the pair travels together in a single mod rather than as two options: the caster buys the clause and then chooses at the cast, exactly as Resistances "any one of its saving throws (selected when casting)" does. fixes.name: Regenerate
fixes.reason: "+1 PP: the casting time is 2 AP (somatic, verbal)" shipped inert. A ONE-MINUTE CAST BECOMES A TWO-ACTION ONE, which under Graham's ruling is the difference between a spell that cannot be cast in a fight at all (1 minute = 30 AP) and one that can - the cheapest warp in the pack, at 1 PP, doing the largest thing in this channel.  THE PARENTHESIS BUYS NOTHING AND NEEDS NO KEY. Regenerate's components are ALREADY somatic and verbal (measured: {somatic:true, verbal:true, material:false, focus:false}), so "(somatic, verbal)" restates what the spell has rather than changing it. A componentsOff-style mod here would have been a key nothing reads.  THE CAST-TIME CHANNEL (3.518.0). Five warps across five spells - Regenerate, Lifekeeping, Restoration, Crackling Tempest, Restore Senses - say some version of "the casting time changes" and every one shipped with mods: {}. Measured before building: those five are the complete set in the pack, and they speak two ways, so there are two keys. `castApSet` REPLACES the printed time; `castApDelta` ADJUSTS it. See magic/cast-time.mjs.  GRAHAM'S RULING, 7 Sep 2026, is what makes the channel worth anything: "Anything with a cast time of more than 3 AP cannot be cast in combat. A combat round is 6 seconds so an AP equates to about 2 seconds. A 1 minute casting would be 30 AP and a 10 minutes casting 300 AP, no combat would ever last that long." Before it, a one-minute cast was read as 1 AP and these warps bought a change nobody could feel.

fixes.name: Fatigue
fixes.reason: "+1 PP: increase the range to 30 feet" shipped inert. Touch out to thirty feet - the cheapest of the ten at 1 PP, and on a spell whose whole risk was having to reach the target.  THE RANGE CHANNEL (3.519.0). 25 warps across 25 spells change how far a spell reaches and every one shipped with mods: {}. ONE KEY, `rangeOverride`, because all 25 SET a new range and not one says "+10 feet per purchase" - an override in the shape of `areaOverride`, not a count in the shape of `areaGrowth`.  THE WARPS ONLY BUY SOMETHING BECAUSE THE SAME RELEASE MADE RANGE MEAN SOMETHING. Measured before building: nothing in the system ever compared a distance to a spell's printed range, so a TOUCH spell landed on a creature across the room. A weapon has refused exactly this since long before - "Toben is 40 ft away - beyond Longsword's reach (max 10 ft)" - so 3.519.0 is one rule reaching the other half of the game. Graham's ruling, 7 Sep 2026: enforce it, and refuse. See magic/spell-range.mjs.

fixes.name: Sudden Sickening
fixes.reason: "+6 PP: you can target up to 10 targets within range" shipped inert. A flat TOTAL on a "1 creature" spell - one to ten, not one plus ten.  THE TARGET-COUNT CHANNEL (3.520.0). 3.498.0 built `extraTargets`, an INCREMENT, for the 46 warps that sell "an additional creature". Measured this release: TWELVE MORE warps name a TOTAL instead - "target up to 10 targets", "target up to 1 creature per level" - and no key could carry one. A total REPLACES the printed cap; an increment adds to it, and folding one into the other would make the printed number mean something different on every spell that bought it. `targetCapFor` combines them and the target-count GATE already calls it, so these buy an enforced permission rather than a printed sentence. See magic/target-count.mjs.

fixes.name: Gentle Repose
fixes.reason: A CORRECTION TO `gentle-repose-unlimited`, ONE STEP EARLIER IN THIS SAME RELEASE, and the sweep is what caught it. "The spell takes one more action to cast" was authored as `castApDelta: 1` because the sentence is phrased relatively - but a DELTA ACCUMULATES, so `warpScalesWithRepeats` reported the warp as repeatable and the chooser drew an UNCAPPED NUMBER BOX for it. `verify-warp-repeats` P2 moved 145 -> 146 and that is what it was telling us: buying this option twice would buy no extra duration (unlimited is already unlimited) and would cost a SECOND extra action. A warp that penalises a repeat purchase is not a warp.  A SET IS THE RIGHT SHAPE: `castApSet` is not multiplied by `times`, so the option goes back to being the checkbox it reads as. Gentle Repose prints castAP 2, so one more action is 3.  THE ARITHMETIC IS NOW IN THE DATA, which is the cost of a set, so `verify-warped-duration` pins it against the spell's own printed cast time rather than against the literal 3 - if the printed cast time ever changes, the check fails instead of the warp quietly meaning something else.

fixes.name: Cure
fixes.reason: "+2 PP: the amount of healing increases by 1d8 and the extra healing for the 2-action version increases by 8." THE SECOND HALF OF GRAHAM'S OWN REPORT of 7 Sep 2026, whose first half (repeatable with no limit) shipped at 3.515.0 and whose bleed clauses shipped at 3.516.0. Bought once, Cure's 2 AP row goes from "1d8 + 8" to "1d8 + 16 + 1d8"; its 1 AP and 3 AP rows print no flat term and gain only the die.  THE AP-ROW EXTRA (3.522.0). Cure and Inflict each print a warp whose SECOND clause names the two-action row's flat bonus, and only the first clause was ever built: `damageDice: "1d8"` added the die and the eight reached nothing. Graham reported it on Cure and it stood open through six releases.  `rowExtra` MULTIPLIES THE ROW'S OWN CONSTANT rather than carrying an 8 of its own. Both spells print exactly 8 on their 2 AP row so the two readings are indistinguishable here; this one keeps the number in ONE place - the AP row's formula - so a row with no flat term is untouched (Cure's 1 AP and 3 AP rows are a bare "1d8") and a row printing something else gets its own. See `warpedRowExtra` in magic/caster-level-mods.mjs.

fixes.name: Magic Weapon
fixes.reason: SPELL-GRANTED POTENCY RUNES (3.523.0). Five spells promise a temporary Potency rune and all five shipped with `effects: []`, so the spell cast, spent PP and posted a card describing a rune nobody received. Each also carries a step warp with `mods: {}` — inert twice over, since it stepped a rune that was never applied.  NOT ONE LINE OF RUNE MACHINERY HAD TO BE WRITTEN, which is the sentence `feats-workflow` wrote about Blade Ally at 3.330.0 and is true again for the same reason: `runes.mjs` already parses the field and takes the highest tier when a rune is named twice, and `rune-effects.mjs` already turns potency into the attack and damage numbers. Writing `system.runes` is the whole mechanism, and the loan is restored by WRITE-BACK of the stored previous field rather than by subtracting our entry — Blade Ally learned that one, where subtracting would strip a rune the player added while imbued.  Magic Weapon: the base rule, which is the half that was missing entirely. Tier I on cast, written onto the chosen item's own `runes` field and taken back when the spell ends.

fixes.name: Word Of Blinding
fixes.reason: AN AREA WARP THAT WAS ONLY EVER PROSE (3.530.0). `areaOverride` has been live and complete since the area work — `warpedAreaText` returns it outright, and twelve warps already use it, ten of them on spells whose own printed area is empty, exactly like these. What was missing on these seven was the mod: the option was offered, its PP was charged, and the spell went on hitting one creature.  TWO THINGS WERE MEASURED BEFORE DECLARING THESE, because either would have made the fix worse than the gap. First, `areaTargeting` is a SPELL-level field read at cast-workflow.mjs:2450 and :3186; all seven are "all", so a warp reading "all creatures" needs nothing further, and Aid's "all allies" needed the new `areaTargetingOverride` or it would have handed temporary HP and +1 to attack to every ENEMY in the radius. Second, every effect row here targets `targets` (or, for Word Of Biting, damage rides `system.damage` as it does on Dark Tendrils' identical override) — a row targeting `self` would have drawn a template that granted nothing to anyone standing in it, which is why Confounded Imagery, Prescience, Hunter's Veil and Concealing Terrain are NOT in this list.

fixes.name: Soothing Ballad
fixes.reason: HEALING RAISED ON ITS OWN SIDE (3.531.0). The heal row has consumed `damageDice` since the bleed channel, and Cure is the precedent: on Cure the healing IS the spell's one number, so a die aimed at 'damage' lands correctly. Soothing Ballad is that same shape and is a pure data fix. Wash Away Sin is NOT: it heals 1d8 and burns 1d6 from one warp reading 'increase both the healing and damage by 1 die', and a single `damageDice` cannot be two die sizes — set it to 1d8 and the damage becomes 1d6 + 1d8. `healDice` names the healing side only and falls back to `damageDice` when absent, so Cure is byte-identical. Make Whole prints a bare '20' and its warp adds five; `rowExtra` multiplies a TRAILING constant and cannot see a bare one, so `healBonus` is the flat sibling.

fixes.name: Luminous Flare
fixes.reason: THREE WARPS WHOSE MOD ALREADY EXISTED (3.531.0). Nothing was built for these — `areaGrowth`/`areaMax`, `extraTargets` and `rangeOverride` have all been live for releases. The sentence was in the pack and the mod was never authored, which is the same defect class as the six Word Of ___ spells at 3.530.0.  SHIELD OF FAITH NEEDED A RULING AND GOT ONE. Its range and targets fields are both BLANK, where every existing `rangeOverride` sits on a spell with a written base range. Graham, 8 September 2026: "Spells that have no range or area affect the caster. So if a warping option increases that to a range (such as touch) then it gains that range with the warping option." A blank range is therefore SELF, not missing data — so this is an ordinary override and not the note-only-base trap. Its row already targets `targets`, which resolves to the caster while the range is blank and to the touched creature once it is not, so nothing else moves.

fixes.name: Ethereal Jaunt
fixes.reason: A REGRESSION 3.532.0 INTRODUCED, REPAIRED (3.533.0). Ethereal Jaunt's warp reads "+1 PP: target an additional willing creature AT A RANGE OF TOUCH" and carries `extraTargets: 1`. Its printed range is blank, which until 3.532.0 meant no limit to enforce — so the extra creature could be targeted from anywhere. Under Graham's ruling a blank range means the caster, and the gate began refusing that creature with "beyond Ethereal Jaunt's range of self" — a refusal of the very thing the warp charges PP to permit.  WHAT THIS FIX IS AND IS NOT. It is a gate repair: `rangeOverride: "touch"` makes the spell reach the distance its own warp names, so the extra target is legal again. It is NOT a claim that the spell does anything to that creature — Ethereal Jaunt has NO effect rows at all (`effects: []`); becoming ethereal lives entirely in its description. That was true before this release and stays true after it. The distinction matters because giving a mod to an unbuilt base is the trap this project has walked into four times, and this is deliberately the other thing: removing a refusal, not inventing an effect.

fixes.name: Invisibility
fixes.reason: THE RULING FINISHES INVISIBILITY (3.533.0). Its warp reads "+1 PP: the spells range becomes touch, and you may target another creature" and had no mod at all — offered, charged, and dropped, like the seven at 3.530.0.  IT NEEDED NO REDIRECT, which is why it is here and Jump and Loremasters Edge are not. Its effect row already targets `targets`, and under the ruling `targets` on a blank-range spell resolves to the caster — so unwarped it turns the caster invisible, exactly as printed, and the override is what lets that same row land on a creature you touch. The two halves of the warp's sentence are one mod because the range IS what changes who it reaches.  Measured: it is one of only two blank-range spells whose rows target `targets` (Shield Of Faith is the other, fixed at 3.531.0), which is why this list is two spells long rather than twenty.

fixes.name: Jump
fixes.reason: A `self` ROW GIVEN SOMEWHERE ELSE TO GO (3.534.0). These warps grant reach to a spell whose only effect row targets `self`, so until now the option was offered, charged, and the effect stayed on the caster — the reach was real and nothing travelled along it.  THESE TWO MOVE IT, and that is read off their own words rather than assumed: Jump says "the target CHANGES to one touched creature" and Loremasters Edge says "TARGET AN ALLY within 30 feet". Both name a different creature INSTEAD of the caster, so `retargetSelfRows` hands the row to whoever the spell reached and the caster keeps nothing. The four spells whose warps say "affects ALL allies" take `shareSelfRows` instead — Graham's ruling of 8 September 2026 was to follow the wording of each warp rather than share one flag, and these are the two halves of that.  The `rangeOverride` beside it is what the same sentence's other clause asks for, and without it the 3.532.0 gate would refuse the very creature the warp names.

fixes.name: Confounded Imagery
fixes.reason: A `self` ROW SHARED, NOT MOVED (3.534.0). Same channel as Jump and Loremasters Edge and the opposite half of it. These four warps grant an area to a spell whose only row targets `self`, and every one of them says the effect reaches MORE people rather than a different person: "affects ALL allies within 30 feet", "YOU affect all allies in a 20-foot radius", "affecting ALL TARGETS within", "a 15-foot radius centred on YOU". Two of them name the caster outright. So `shareSelfRows` keeps the caster and adds everyone the area caught, counting them once.  THE AREA NEEDS NO EMANATION WORDING. `placeSpellTemplate` already centres a circle on the caster when the spell prints no range (spell-template.mjs: "No-range circle / emanation: drop it on the caster"), which is exactly what "centred on you" means — measured rather than assumed, so the override says what the book says.  HUNTER'S VEIL AND PRESCIENCE ALSO TAKE `areaTargetingOverride: "allies"`, because they say allies and the spells are `areaTargeting: "all"`. Without it they would hand their concealment and their bonus to the enemies standing in the circle — the exact defect Aid was saved from at 3.530.0.

fixes.name: Elven Chainmail
fixes.reason: NOBODY COULD WEAR IT (3.536.0). Its `category` was the literal string "armour" rather than a tier, so the Light/Medium/Heavy lookup missed and the named lookup missed, and the rule fell through to "not proficient with armour armour" — a message whose doubled word is the tell. Not a Wizard problem: a FIGHTER with proficiency in all armour was refused it too, and would have taken -4 and doubled check penalties for wearing his own magic armour. Found by widening the proficiency cross-product to the packs it had never loaded. Tier read off the base table by DR, penalty, max Dex and weight; the two that did not read cleanly went to Graham, 9 Sep 2026.

fixes.name: Scale
fixes.reason: SCALE IS NOT METAL (3.536.0). Graham's ruling, 9 Sep 2026. The Ranger and the Druid both print "non-metal" and both are granted Scale by name, while Scale itself shipped material "Metal" and the Metal trait — so the printed sentence and the table contradicted each other on one item. Ruled in favour of the classes: this Scale is hide and scale plate rather than scale mail. Found when the proficiency cross-product was widened to every pack and the metal/non-metal split was asserted as a RULE instead of a pinned pair of names.  CONSEQUENCE WORTH KNOWING: anything else keying off the Metal trait — rust, corrosion, spells that grip metal — stops treating Scale as metal too. That is the same ruling, applied consistently, and it is the reason this is two rows rather than a special case inside the proficiency table.

fixes.name: Dead Tongue
fixes.reason: A FIXED DURATION REPLACES SUSTAINING (3.538.0). Graham's ruling, 9 Sep 2026, after live testing showed the result card printing both "the duration changes until next daily preparation" AND "Sustained — Sustain it each turn to maintain it" about the same cast. The contradiction was older than the warps built at 3.537.0: the 1-hour rung, built long before, printed it too.  `endsSustain` is new vocabulary at this release and is read by sustainAfterWarp() in active-spells.mjs, which four call sites now share — the banner, the registry entry the Spellcasting panel reads, the `ends` clock, and the orphan-sweep predicate. Dropping the banner alone would have left a sustain entry in the panel for a spell whose card never mentioned it. NOT APPLIED to Lifekeeping's "1 minute (S)" rung or to Project Image, whose text says "the maximum duration you can SUSTAIN the Spell increases" — both raise the cap rather than ending the sustaining, and both say so in their own wording.

fixes.name: Word Of Stunning
fixes.reason: THE STRONGEST PRECEDENT IN THE WHOLE SURVEY (3.539.0). Word Of Blinding's warp carries the SAME SENTENCE, character for character — "the spell effects all creatures in a 20 feet radius" — at the same 4 PP, on a spell with the same 30-foot range and the same "1 creature" target line, and it has been built as areaOverride: "20-foot radius" for releases. This one was simply never filled in.  `areaOverride` is read at CAST level, not from an effect row, so the fact that Word Of Stunning carries only a `note` row where Word Of Blinding carries `condition, note` does not block it — that distinction is what the 3.539.0 survey work exists to check, and it was checked here.

fixes.name: Dead Tongue
fixes.reason: "ADD ONE TARGET" (3.539.0), against Banishment's built "per additional target" → extraTargets: 1. Dead Tongue prints "1 spirit or undead" as its target line, so one more is exactly what the sentence asks for and exactly what the mod does. `extraTargets` is read at cast level and needs no effect row, which matters because this spell has none.  REVERTED at 3.539.0, before shipping. `warpMaxTimes` returns Infinity for this shape, so "add one target" would have become an UNCAPPED repeatable at 1 PP each — the warp-repeats ratchet caught the count moving and that is what it is for. Banishment's precedent reads "PER additional target", which licenses repetition; Dead Tongue's reads "add ONE target", which does not obviously license anything beyond one. That is a ruling for Graham, not a reading for me.

fixes.name: Dead Tongue
fixes.reason: Puts Dead Tongue's "add one target" back to inert until the repeat question is ruled on. An inert warp is a known gap; an uncapped one is a silent change to what a spell costs to scale, which is worse than the gap it was fixing.  RULED at 3.540.0: Graham, 9 Sep 2026 — "Dead Tongue - 1 additional target per PP". So the uncapped repeat this revert was protecting against is the intended behaviour, and the option goes back in. The revert was still right to happen: the difference between "once" and "per PP" is a spell's scaling economy, and it was not mine to decide from the word "one".

fixes.name: Dead Tongue
fixes.reason: "ADD ONE TARGET" IS PER PP (3.540.0). Graham's ruling, 9 Sep 2026: "Dead Tongue - 1 additional target per PP".  `extraTargets: 1` with no cap is exactly that — `warpMaxTimes` returns Infinity for this shape, so the chooser draws a COUNT BOX rather than a checkbox and each additional PP buys one more spirit or undead. Built at 3.539.0, reverted the same release when the warp-repeats ratchet showed the count moving, and restored here now the scaling is confirmed rather than assumed. Banishment's "per additional target" carries the same mod and reads the same way.

fixes.name: Shield

from.text: Enables the Shield Block reaction (base DR 1 + BSB); after a Shield Block the spell ends and can't be recast for 10 minutes.

fixes.reason: THE SPELL DID NOT DO THE THING IT IS NAMED FOR (3.542.0). Graham's ruling, 9 Sep 2026: these should become real rows.  MEASURED FIRST: `shieldBlockEligibility` filters for `item.type === "shield" && equipped`, so a caster with Shield up and nothing on their arm got `able: false, why: "no shield is equipped"` — while this very note promised a Shield Block. The spell gave +1 defence and nothing else.  NOT A CONJURED ITEM, and that is the whole design: the DR is "1 + BSB", so it scales with the caster and no item can carry it. A conjured shield would be wrong at every level but one. The new `spellShield` row keeps the base and the scaling apart, and shield-block.mjs now weighs a spell-made shield against a carried one on the same best-of-them rule.  THE NOTE IS REPLACED, NOT KEPT BESIDE THE ROW. Leaving both would be the Wash Away Sin shape again — prose next to mechanism, saying the same thing, free to drift apart.

fixes.name: Shield
fixes.reason: "INCREASE SHIELD BONUS & BASE DR BY +1 (MAX +5)" (3.542.0), against Veiled Presence's built "increase the bonus by 1 (max +5)".  THIS WARP WAS UNBUILDABLE UNTIL THE ROW ABOVE EXISTED. It names two things and the second — base DR — lived in a note, so building it would have raised the defence bonus and silently dropped the DR. That is the half-sentence defect this session has now hit three times.  ONE MOD RAISES BOTH HALVES deliberately: the `bonus` row and the `spellShield` row both read `bonusValue`, because the spell's own sentence binds them together. A separate DR key would let them drift.

fixes.name: Eldritch Weapon
fixes.reason: THE SPELL HAD NO EFFECT ROWS AT ALL (3.543.0). Graham's ruling, 9 Sep 2026: these should become real rows.  "You create a one-handed simple melee weapon of pure magic sized appropriately for you... The weapon requires any usual proficiencies but inflicts force damage rather than its normal type." `effects: []`. Six PP produced nothing, and all three warping options were inert because there was no weapon for any of them to modify — which is why the potency warp read as BUILDABLE in the survey and was not.  NOT `conjureItem`: that row names one entry and copies it (Bless Water → Holy Water). This spell names a CLASS and the caster picks, so the row carries a FILTER — one-handed, melee, Simple — and the workflow asks. Widened to Martial by the first warp.  DAMAGE TYPE IS A REPLACEMENT, not an addition: "rather than its normal type" means a conjured mace does no bludgeoning at all.

fixes.name: Eldritch Weapon
fixes.reason: "THE WEAPON CAN BE A MARTIAL WEAPON" (3.543.0). `weaponCategories` is new vocabulary at this release and WIDENS rather than replaces — "can be" leaves the simple weapons on the table, and no warp in the pack takes away something already paid for.  This warp could not be built until the row above existed; there was no choice list to widen.

fixes.name: Enigma
fixes.reason: ENIGMA SAYS IT AND NOTHING READ IT. "You are an Instinctive caster (see Chapter 9) and do not have to memorise your spells during daily preparation." Measured on a level-12 Wizard holding the feat: casterStyle was still `learned` and memorisationStyle still `book`, so the repertoire card — gated on "instinctive" — never appeared and three of the feat archetype’s four promises were inert. `casterStyle` is the field a CLASS already used to declare this; at 3.547.0 any owned item may declare it (magic/caster-style.mjs), and this row is Enigma declaring it.

fixes.name: Halfling
fixes.reason: Page 14's Race Table is printed with size already folded in — 'any size modifiers to ability scores and hit points are included in the above values' — and the system applies the Creature Size Modifiers table itself, in actor.mjs, to every actor with a size. For the two Small races that meant Str -1 and Dex +1 were applied TWICE: once by the size table and again by this effect, which carried the full printed line. Measured by running resolveBonuses over a built actor on 10 September 2026: a Halfling resolved Str -2 / Dex +3 against a printed -1 / +2, and a Gnome Str -2 / Dex +2 against a printed -1 / +1. Every Halfling and Gnome in the world has been wrong since the size table was wired in. The intended design was never in doubt - the race items' own descriptions say in as many words that the effect applies 'only the remainder', and the 3.193.0 release notes record Graham's ruling of 2 August 2026 and a harness check that racial + size = printed. Both the data and that check were lost since. This restores the remainder, and tools/verify-chapter1.mjs re-pins the rule for all eight races so it cannot drift again. Medium races are unaffected: their size modifiers are 0.

fixes.name: Forbidden Magic
fixes.reason: Forbidden Magic prints three clauses and the third is its own: 'must also make a Will saving throw against beneficial spells of these traditions when cast upon you.' Until 3.552.0 that clause was inferred from the `forbiddenTraditions` flag - the flag that means 'cannot cast' - with no test of which feature declared it. The Nerini gnome heritage carries that same flag for a different printed rule, 'you can never be an ethereal or verdant spell caster', which says nothing about receiving anything. Measured in Graham's world on 10 September 2026: a Nerini healed by a verdant ally had to pass a Will save for the healing to be allowed to work, under a rule they do not have. beneficialSaveTraditionsOf now reads THIS flag, so the clause belongs to the ability that prints it. Found by the pages 18-30 audit.

fixes.name: Sorini
fixes.reason: Sorini prints 'You gain a scent as a secondary sense' and granted nothing at all: racialAbilities and grantedFeats were both empty, so applyAllGrants had nothing to apply. Its only carrier was a featNote effect reading 'There is no senses model yet, so this is adjudicated at the table' - which stopped being true when the Chapter 8 senses model was built. The abilities pack already contains a correctly wired Scent ability (category secondary, modality olfactory, special) used today by animal companions; naming it here lands the sense on the sheet with a computed range and makes it reachable by Enhanced-modality feats. TWO PRINTED CONFLICTS REMAIN, flagged to Graham rather than decided here: Chapter 8 says a creature sensed only by a secondary sense is HIDDEN, while Sorini prints 'exact location'; and the printed downwind/upwind doubling and halving has no representation in senseRangeFeet. Found by the pages 18-30 audit.

fixes.name: Wild Stride
fixes.reason: Wild Stride's terrain easing shipped correct and complete in passive-feats.mjs, and was gated on the FEAT NAME 'wild stride' — featNames is built from feat items only. The Silvarni elf heritage prints the same rule word for word ('ignore all natural difficult terrain. Furthermore, natural formidable terrain is classed as difficult terrain for you') and could never reach it under any name; it carried a featNote saying terrain costs are not modelled, which was false. At 3.552.0 the rule is keyed on flags.trg-prime.ignoresDifficultTerrain across items AND effects, so a feat, a heritage, a spell or an item can all carry it. This row sets the flag on the two things that print the rule today. Found by the pages 18-30 audit.

fixes.name: Gnome Resistance
fixes.reason: Gnome Resistance prints 'You may use a reaction when targeted by A SPELL to gain advantage to the saving throw.' The offer seam fires on every type:'save' roll in the system and the only scoping was the save TYPE and the area exemption, so a Gnome was offered the reaction on a poison affliction, a falling save, an exhaustion save and a trap. saveAdvantageDecision gained a spellOnly gate at 3.552.0, tested against whether cast-workflow set saveSource — the one writer of it. Declared only on this entry: Juggernaut, Evasion and Resolve print no such trigger and keep the any-source behaviour. Found by the pages 18-30 audit.

fixes.name: Storgar
fixes.to: +2 racial bonus to resist being shoved or moved involuntarily — judge whether it applies here.
fixes.reason: Storgar prints '+2 racial bonus to all checks to resist being shoved or moved involuntarily'. Shove already applies it, on the defender's Fortitude DC, per Graham's ruling of 16 Aug 2026 — but Shove is the only forced-movement route in the system with a DC to attach it to. A critical-table push and a spell's forced movement move the token with no contest at all, so the printed clause reached neither, and the heritage carried a featNote nobody reads. Graham ruled on 10 Sep 2026 (R6, pages 18-30 audit): 'create this as a text prompt for the character… Each situation should be gauged at the time and there are far too many variables.' This flag is that prompt: forced-movement.mjs collects it and the push buttons carry it, so the sentence is in front of the table at the moment the push is offered rather than after the token has moved.

to.label: Ethnicity Lore
to.prompt: The ethnicity you were raised in

fixes.reason: Page 28 gives the Human a specialist skill: 'lore based upon your ethnicity… (Hill Man Lore) or… (Urban Lore)'. Human.system.specialistSkills was empty and nothing else produced it, so the one race whose printed lore is a CHOICE was the one race that never got a lore at all. Every other race fills that field with literal names. The specialistChoice mechanism eight backgrounds already use (Apprentice, Hermit, Highwayman, Scout, Templar, Cultist, Archaeologist, Scholar) fits it exactly: Apply Grants names the choice on the card, the Use button asks for the answer, and the skill leaves with the race. Found by the pages 18-30 audit (D3).

fixes.name: Wash Away Sin
fixes.reason: GRAHAM'S RULING, 15 September 2026 (R3 of the block-2 follow-ups): "This is an odd one from the rulebook and not sure why I went d8 for the heal and d6 for the damage. I think the easiest thing to do is run d8 on both (including base damage)." So the spell's damage side becomes 1d8, matching its healing, and the +2 PP warp adds one die to each. THIS ROW REPLACES A CONTRADICTORY PAIR: wash-away-sin-both-dice set the warp's mods to {healDice:'1d8', damageDice:'1d6'} and wash-away-sin-revert set them straight back to {}, so the two fought on every run of apply-data-fixes — it reported '2 applied' for ever and rewrote the spell twice per run, while the warp itself did nothing. Both are retired here and their history is recorded in this reason rather than in two rows that undo each other. Found by the pages 18-30 fix pass, ruled on 15 Sep 2026. THE WARP ITSELF IS DELIBERATELY LEFT INERT: verify-warped-healing D3 pins warps.0.mods as EMPTY, because the {healDice, damageDice} version shipped at 3.531.0 and was reverted at 3.531.1 after live testing — not over the dice sizes, but because the spell is areaTargeting 'allies', so its damage can only ever land on the allies it exists to heal, and the 'creatures with an opposed aura' condition lives in a note that nothing tests. Adding a die doubles a number that is hitting the wrong people. Graham's R3 ruling settles the DICE; the targeting question is separate and still open.

fixes.name: Shadow Stance
fixes.reason: The ability's printed block reads 'SHADOW STANCE / OPEN STANCE / Action 1 AP' — and OPEN STANCE is its TRAITS LINE, not a second ability. The pages 18-30 audit read it as a missing feature ('Open Stance has no representation at all'); Graham corrected that on 15 Sep 2026: "I have no Open Stance ability in the rules. Shadow Stance has Open and Stance as traits!" The correction exposed a real defect: system.traits was EMPTY, so both printed traits reached nothing. The system models both — traits.mjs gates an Open action to being your first action of the turn (line 139) and makes a Stance wait a round before another Stance (line 194) — and neither could fire on the one ability in the pack that prints them.

fixes.name: Wash Away Sin
fixes.reason: GRAHAM'S RULING, 15 September 2026, on how Wash Away Sin's damage side should work. The spell prints "Allies in the cone regain 1d8 HP... Creatures with an opposed aura take 1d8 essence damage", and until now the cone was areaTargeting 'allies' — so the damage could only ever land on the allies the spell exists to heal, which is why verify-warped-healing D3 refused to arm its warp. Offered three ways out (build the opposed-aura test, drop the damage clause, or leave it to the table) he chose the first: "Needs to be option 1." Three rows carry it: the cone catches everyone; the heal row is narrowed to allies so it still only heals your own side; and the damage declares the opposed-aura scope that magic/damage-scope.mjs now implements. The warp's mods stay EMPTY until this has been driven at a table — the dice were never the problem.

fixes.name: Scrying
fixes.reason: GRAHAM'S RULING, 15 September 2026, taking the recommendation offered after live testing 3.552.8. Primal Warrior prints a bonus ATTACK/SAVE spell, and the chooser now reads system.category to find them. Eight spells sat as category 'utility' while carrying a defence, so they resolved as save spells at the table — the cast engine decides that from the defence, not the category — while being labelled utility for spell-scoped conditionals and left off every attack/save list. Offered three ways out (leave them off, widen the filter to 'category OR defence', or correct the data) he took the third: "Please use your recommendation for both issues." These four target an unwilling creature who resists the spell aimed at it, which is what a save spell is; the other four — Unremarkable Aura, Solitude, Rainbow Cloak, Verdant Retribution — stay utility, because their save belongs to somebody interacting with an area rather than to the target of the spell.
