fixes.name: Druid
fixes.reason: ERRATUM E2 from the audit of pages 41-50, amended by Graham in the rulebook on 15 September 2026: "I have amended the errata in my rulebook." The Druid entry printed its key abilities with the comma INSIDE the requirement - "Constitution, (min +2), Dexterity, Wisdom" - where every other class prints "Constitution (min +2)". The pack copied the line verbatim, so it was cosmetic while nothing read it. R1 of the same audit made something read it: classAbilityRequirement takes the subject of the requirement to be whatever sits between the previous comma and the bracket, so the broken line names nothing and the parser REFUSES it - a Druid got no minimum-ability warning at all while every other class did. The parser still refuses that shape deliberately (guessing would be worse), and this fix removes the only line in the pack with it.

fixes.name: Fighter
fixes.reason: GRAHAM'S RULING R1, 16 September 2026, on the TRG Prime 3.8 rulebook revision. The Fighter and Rogue tables printed "-" in Caster Level and PP at every level, and the system stored that as null — an absence, not a zero. The revision changes all forty cells in each table to 0, and no dash remains in any class table anywhere in the book. Asked whether 0 is a real zero or the book's new way of writing "not applicable", he answered: "Yes make it a real 0." So the cell is a zero. The two places that read the null as "this class does not cast" — the PP ability bonus and resolvedCasterLevel — now ask whether the CLASS declares a magical ability, which is the thing they always meant and which the Fighter and Rogue leave empty. Behaviour at the table is unchanged; what changes is that the cell can be added to.

fixes.name: Martial Artist
fixes.from:
You attended either an elite school, were part of a monastery or were trained by a master. The skills that you were granted will never leave you as you move on to greater things.

BACKGROUND MECHANICS

Bonus feat: Weapon Focus (Unarmed).

+1 class bonus to Acrobatics, Meditation, Mental Focus.

The Weapon Focus choice is made for you: Unarmed — the Brawling group, where unarmed strikes and natural attacks live.

Specialist skill: Combat Styles.
fixes.to:
You attended either an elite school, were part of a monastery or were trained by a master. The skills that you were granted will never leave you as you move on to greater things.

BACKGROUND MECHANICS

Bonus feat: Weapon Focus (Brawling).

+1 class bonus to Acrobatics, Meditation, Mental Focus.

The Weapon Focus choice is made for you: Brawling, the group where unarmed strikes and natural attacks live.

Specialist skill: Combat Styles.
fixes.reason: The 3.8 rulebook revision, read 16 September 2026, prints "Weapon Focus (Brawling)" where 3.7 printed "(Unarmed)". That divergence was errata R4 of 15 September 2026 — there is no Unarmed weapon group, and unarmed strikes live in Brawling — and Graham has now fixed the book. The pack already granted Weapon Focus qualified to Brawling; only this description still quoted the old printing and explained a mapping the book no longer needs. Mechanics unchanged.

fixes.name: Outrider
fixes.from:
The rush of the wind through your hair as you gallop across the plains is a real rush. You once served as a forward scout for your people, but they are long since gone. Now you look to explore new places, but that rush will never fade.

BACKGROUND MECHANICS

Bonus feat: Born to Ride.

+1 class bonus to Handle Animal, Perception, Survival.

Specialist skill: Plains Lore.

The book prints this row as Terrain Lore (Plains).

fixes.name: Druid
fixes.from:
You are more than just a priest of nature. You belong to an ancient order of verdant magic. Druids are often found amongst tribal societies acting as priests, healers, lore master's and law givers. As a Druid, you seek to preserve the natural balance of things.

Play a Druid if you want to be one with Nature and help your companions with your wise counsel and healing skills.

Class Type Adept

Key Ability Scores Constitution, (min +2), Dexterity, Wisdom

Proficiencies You are proficient with any non-metal armour or shield. You may use any non-metal weapon.

Class Skills Athletics, Climbing, Culture, Handle Animal, Linguistics, Meditation, Mental Focus, Nature, Power Manipulation, Survival

Skill Points 6 + Int per level

Hit Points 6 + Con per level

Bonus Feats At 1st level you gain the Heighten Spell feat and the Wild Stride Feat.

Magical Tradition You are a verdant, learned spell caster and may select your Spell Lists from the Verdant Tradition. To cast your spells, you must spend time in communion with nature during your daily preparation. This process usually takes about half an hour and must be carried out in an outdoor rural or wilderness environment (GM discretion). At the end of this time, you may select an amount of spells for which you meet the casting requirements, from the Verdant Spell List to commit to memory for the day equal to 2 + (level x 2). Spells committed to memory may be cast using your Power Points (Chapter 9: Magic).

Magical Ability Score Your constitution is your magical ability score. You add your Con to your Spellcraft bonus and as a static bonus to your PP.

Specialist Spells You gain any one PP 1 Druid Specialist Spell at 1st level. You may learn additional Druid Specialist Spells by purchasing the Specialist Skill Feat.

Cantrips Each day when you prepare your spells you may also learn any four verdant cantrips. You may select your cantrips from the Verdant spell list and may change them each day during daily preparation.

Class Abilities Wild Empathy (1st level), Wild Shape (3rd level), Druidic Code (1st level)

fixes.name: Conjure Plant
fixes.reason: Graham reported on 17 September 2026, from his own session: "The sheet only allows the warping option to be applied once. This warping should be allowed multiple times (the same with the other conjure spells)." All nine conjure spells sell "+1 PP: increase the max level of the creature by 1 (to a maximum of your caster level)" and all nine carried mods: {}. warpScalesWithRepeats asks the aggregator whether a second purchase changes anything; with no mods there was nothing to change, so buildWarpChooser drew a checkbox and a 20th-level caster could raise the creature one level and no further. conjuredLevel is the increment; conjuredBase is this spell's own printed ceiling, taken verbatim from its description — "This plant must be 1st level or lower." — rather than parsed out of it, because the nine descriptions phrase that ceiling six different ways and a reworded revision would silently drop a spell back to a checkbox. See magic/conjured-creature.mjs; asserted against the printed descriptions by verify-conjure-warp.

fixes.name: Restoration
fixes.from:
You channel healing energy into the target over the course of the spell duration. This reduces the fatigued condition by 1.
Be aware this spell removes the penalty but does not necessarily repair permanent damage such as missing body parts and does not stop bleeding or other conditions. Furthermore, a creature may only benefit from one restoration spell each day.
HEALING MISCELLANOUS INJURIESSome critical injuries will leave a penalty without an attached condition. If this is the case, the injury can be healed using the Restoration spell. In this case, each severity level of the injury is considered to be the Injured 1 condition for healing purposes.Be aware that if a specific spell (such as Regenerate) can be used to heal an injury, then Restoration cannot be used.HEALING MISCELLANOUS INJURIESSome critical injuries will leave a penalty without an attached condition. If this is the case, the injury can be healed using the Restoration spell. In this case, each severity level of the injury is considered to be the Injured 1 condition for healing purposes.Be aware that if a specific spell (such as Regenerate) can be used to heal an injury, then Restoration cannot be used.

Warping Options:
+1 PP: instead reduce the dazed or weakened conditions by 1.
+2 PP: instead reduce the injured condition by 1.
+2 PP: increase the amount of a condition reduced by 1 (or 5 for soul drain).
+4 PP: instead cure 5 points of soul drain.
+5 PP: cast time changes to 3 AP.
+6 PP: instead reduce the Doomed Condition.

fixes.reason: A SIDEBAR THE IMPORT READ TWICE. Word stores a text box twice in document.xml — once under mc:Choice for modern readers and again under mc:Fallback (a v:textbox) for old ones — and the extraction that built this pack walked every <w:t>, so it read every sidebar in the rulebook twice. 2,274 of the book's 75,245 <w:t> elements sit inside a Fallback: 85 text boxes, 33k characters. FOUND ON 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 WHEN GRAHAM CORRECTED MY OWN ERRATA. The pages 91-100 audit reported NEGATIVE PP (p91) and FEAT VS FEAT (p100) as printed twice in the book; his reply was "E1 and E2 are not duplicated", and he was right — my extractor doubled them. tools/pages.py now skips mc:Fallback. This fix removes the same doubling where it reached the shipped pack data. The sidebar is kept once; only the second copy goes, and the from/to guard refuses if the text has moved since.

fixes.name: Mage Armour
fixes.from:
You enhance your armour or clothing with magical energy causing it to ripple slightly. Whilst this spell is in effect, your clothing hardens and grants you Armour DR 1 with 20 HP. If the armour is reduced to 0 Hits, it is destroyed and the spell cannot be cast again for 1 hour.

Warping Options:
+2 PP: the duration changes to until your next daily preparations.
+4 PP: the DR increases by +1.

Caster Level Modifications:
CL 4+: The armour HP increase by 20.
CL 6+: Armour DR multiplier increases by 1.
CL 8+: The armour also grants CR 1
CL 10: the armour is considered to be rigid for injury purposes.
MAGE ARMOUR & INCREASING DRJust as armour DR increases as a non-casters BDB increases, the bonus gained from this spell also increases based upon the casters BSB.So a Wizard with a BSB of 6, would gain DR 2 from the unmodified casting of this spell. fixes.name: Shape Of The Aberrant
fixes.from:
You warp your body and mind into a vessel of unfathomable alien essence, shifting into a medium aberrant form. While in your aberrant form:
You gain the Aberration and Polymorph traits.
You gain Darkvision and Telepathy (constantly as the spell)
You lose the ability to speak, but you may still cast spells that do not have a verbal component.
You retain your mental ability scores.
Your gear merges into the form and becomes inaccessible. Any static magical bonuses remain, but non-magical gear no longer provides a bonus.
You gain temporary HP equal to the 3x the PP cost of the spell.
You gain +2 to Fortitude Saving Throws.
You gain an appropriate natural attack (tentacle, claw, bite, pseudopod, etc.). Natural attacks automatically gain the Magical trait.
You may not use weapon or item-based abilities.
Choose one aberrant base form when casting:
Mind Leech: Str +0, Dex +2; Speed: 30 ft.; DR 1
Gain Psychic Lash Attack (range 30 ft) uses BSB to attack if higher than BAB, 1d10+5 damage
Chitin Horror: Str +3, Dex +1: Speed 25 ft; DR 3
FORM SPELLSWhen using a Form spell, you gain racial modifiers and numerous other abilities. These replace any existing physical abilities you already have and racial ability scores are also replaced. If a Form spell alters your size, these modifiers are in addition to any ability score modifiers shown in the stat block.All damage and DR is base and modified for BAB/BDB accordingly. When using a form spell you may choose the appearance of any creature of the appropriate type. This has no bearing upon the abilities you gain from the spell, but may assist you in other ways.FORM SPELLSWhen using a Form spell, you gain racial modifiers and numerous other abilities. These replace any existing physical abilities you already have and racial ability scores are also replaced. If a Form spell alters your size, these modifiers are in addition to any ability score modifiers shown in the stat block.All damage and DR is base and modified for BAB/BDB accordingly. When using a form spell you may choose the appearance of any creature of the appropriate type. This has no bearing upon the abilities you gain from the spell, but may assist you in other ways.

Warping Options:
+1 PP: increase the duration to 10 minutes
+1 PP: gain an additional natural attack (max of two additional attacks).
+1 PP: add Climb 20 ft., Burrow 15 ft., or Swim 30 ft.
+2 PP: increase a movement speed by 10 ft.
+2 PP: increase temporary HP to 4x PP cost of spell.
+2 PP: gain resistance to a physical type of your choice (slashing, piercing, or bludgeoning).
+2 PP: add Fly 30 ft.
+2 PP: add an aberrant trait (see Appendix, max 3).
+4 PP: you may increase or decrease the size of the form by one step.
+6 PP: you may increase or decrease the size of the form by two steps.

fixes.name: Dracoris

to.label: Dracoris
to.scope: Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidate and Sense Motive against a creature of the Wyrm type

to.label: Dracoris (target not known to the roll)
to.scope: Tick if this social check is an interaction with a creature of the Wyrm type

fixes.reason: Printed (Chapter 5, p.104): "You gain a +1 racial bonus to all interactions with creatures of the Wyrm type. Furthermore, your skin has a slightly toughened outer layer increasing your DR by 1." The DR half has always worked - an effect with changes[0] system.combat.dr.race +1. The interactions half shipped as a featNote effect whose description told the player to "queue via the Use button", and there is no Use handler for Dracoris: a printed instruction to press a button that does nothing, which is the same class of defect as a source comment describing behaviour the system does not have. THE RULING (Graham, 17 September 2026) fixed "all interactions" to the four social skills - Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidate, Sense Motive - because "literally any check" would have made it a manual modifier and the audit asked rather than guessed. THE AXIS DID NOT EXIST. `sourceTypes` (3.321.0, Thengar's "+1 against the attacks of creatures of the Undead Type") is the type of whoever PROVOKED the check; this rule needs the type of whoever the check is AIMED AT, and authoring it on sourceTypes would have fired when a Wyrm attacked the Dracoris and never when the Dracoris spoke to one - the wrong answer, quietly. 3.567.0 built `targetTypes` as the fourth corner of the who-provokes/who-is-aimed-at by category/by-uuid matrix, filled from creatureTypesOf(targetActor.system) at the action and attack workflows and accepted by the dialog. TWO ROWS, THE FIRE-LIKE BLOOD SHAPE. The first is `auto` because targeting a Wyrm settles the whole scope with no judgement left. The second is the manual fallback for a social check rolled with no target - a bare Diplomacy from the sheet - and it STANDS DOWN via the `*` wildcard the moment the roll knows what it is aimed at, so the bonus can never be taken twice. A non-Wyrm target offers neither row, which is the point of knowing.

fixes.name: Dracoris
fixes.from: +1 racial bonus to all interactions with Wyrm-type creatures — queue via the Use button.
fixes.to: +1 racial bonus on Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidate and Sense Motive against creatures of the Wyrm type. Applied automatically when a Wyrm is targeted; offered as a tick-box on an untargeted social check.
fixes.reason: The note told the player to "queue via the Use button" and Dracoris has no Use handler - it is registered in none of feats-workflow.mjs's handlers, so the button did nothing and said nothing. An instruction on the sheet to press a control that does not exist is worse than silence, because the player concludes they did it wrong. Rewritten to describe what the conditional authored in dracoris-wyrm-affinity-conditional actually does, including the case where it is offered rather than applied. The effect keeps its featNote marker: it carries no changes and is a printed reminder, which is exactly what that marker means - the MECHANISM now lives on the item, where every one of the pack's other 39 authored conditionals lives.

Applied automatically by Hybrid Transformation's Use button; ends when the ten minutes run out or when you return to humanoid form, whichever comes first. No Power Points are spent.

An instruction on the sheet to press a control that does not exist is worse than silence, because the player concludes they did it wrong. Rewritten to describe what the automation actually does. AND REWRITTEN AGAIN AT 3.567.2, folded into this same row rather than chained behind it: the 3.567.0 wording said the growth ends when you return to humanoid form, which stopped being the whole truth when 3.567.1 gave it its own ten-minute clock - and the half it omitted is the one that ends the effect while the player is still a beast. It now also states that no Power Points are spent, because the printed text names a PP cost and a player reading their untouched pool should not have to guess which of the two is wrong. The effect keeps its featNote marker: it carries no changes and is a printed reminder, which is exactly what that marker means - the MECHANISM lives on the item and in module/hulking-form.mjs.

fixes.from:

fixes.to:
In your hybrid shape, you transform into a formidable and imposing beast.

While in your hybrid form, you gain the effects of the Size Alteration spell (at base PP cost for 10 minutes), enhancing your physical attributes and granting you additional reach and power.
fixes.reason: ERRATUM E4, RULED, AND THE FULL CORRECTED SENTENCE. The printed text cited "the Enlarge spell", and there is no Enlarge spell in TRG Prime - the word appeared exactly twice in 3.8.1 and both were this feat, and it was in no pack. Graham confirmed on 17 September 2026: "E4 should be Size Alteration", and then supplied the whole corrected sentence, which also carries "(at base PP cost for 10 minutes)". DECLARED AS ONE EDIT ON PURPOSE. It was applied in two: the name at 3.567.1, the parenthesis at 3.567.2 after live testing found the pack naming the right spell and omitting the clause that gives the effect its duration. Two rows would have left the first declaring a `to` the second overwrote, which this file refuses on every run thereafter - correctly, and noisily, forever. The history is here instead, where it is read. Size Alteration is the spell whose text the feat describes clause for clause; module/hulking-form.mjs implements its base effect with the ten-minute duration this sentence grants. THE PACK IS CORRECTED AHEAD OF THE BOOK on purpose: the pack is what a player reads at the table, and leaving it pointing at a spell that cannot be looked up is the same defect as the note effect that told them to press a Use button that did not exist.

fixes.name: Assassin
fixes.reason: DEFECT D1 OF THE BLOCK-11 AUDIT (pages 111-120, 18 September 2026). `system.progressionRequirements` is what module/archetype-progression.mjs gates on: you may normally progress only ONE archetype at a time, and taking a second requires satisfying your current one's printed requirement first. An EMPTY field is treated as 'nothing to check' and never blocks - which is the right default for a requirement the parser cannot read, and the wrong answer entirely for one that was simply never extracted. This archetype printed a requirement and carried an empty field, so it had no progression gate at all. HOW IT SURVIVED, recorded because it is the interesting half: archetype-progression.mjs's own header stated as settled fact that Assassin, Enigma, Gymnast and Mastermind 'print no Progression Requirements sentence at all'. Three quarters of that was false against 3.8.1, and anyone checking the four would read the comment, find the empty fields agreeing with it, and stop. The comment was not merely wrong, it was load-bearing for the wrong answer. It has been corrected in the same release, and verify-chapter5-archetype-111-120 now reads these three requirements out of the pack and RUNS them, so the claim cannot rot again. ASSASSIN'S IS AN AND, and the book says so twice - 'and', and 'both'. The parser knew only the OR shape (Loremaster's seven-skill list), so 3.568.0 added `skillAll` beside `skillAny`. Graham's ruling of 18 September 2026: 'R1 build AND'. Reading it as an OR would have halved the requirement, and nobody would ever have noticed, because a gate that opens too early looks exactly like a gate that is satisfied.

fixes.name: Feather Step
fixes.reason: FEATHER STEP (Chapter 5, page 133): "You can Step into difficult terrain as if it was normal terrain." The pages 131-140 audit found it note-only with a finished mechanism one import away - the THIRD time an audit has found that shape (Silvarni at pages 18-30, Terrain Mastery at pages 51-60). The blanket flag `ignoresDifficultTerrain` was NOT the right carrier: it eases every move, and this feat eases one action, so authoring it that way would have been one row and three-quarters of a rule the book does not print. Graham ruled SCOPED on 18 September 2026. At 3.570.0 `ignoresDifficultTerrain(actor, movementKey)` reads this array of armed movement action keys, and the movement workflow passes the armed key in. THE PROHIBITION FALLS OUT OF THE COST and needs no separate permission: a Step is capped at 5 feet of COST, difficult ground doubles the cost, so a 5-foot Step into it costs 10 and is refused by validateArmedMove - relieve the cost and the same check passes. The note effect stays, exactly as Wild Stride's did: it is a printed reminder, not a substitute.

fixes.name: Animal Companion
fixes.reason: PRINTED, pages 137 and unchanged between rulebook revisions 3.8 and 3.8.1: "An animal companion gains 2 skill points plus wisdom ability score per level which it may spend in the same way as that of a PC." The class item was authored with 4, and module/companion.mjs carried a matching COMPANION_SKILL_POINTS = 4 above a doc comment quoting "An animal companion gains 4 skill points per level" - a sentence that appears in NEITHER revision. Two wrong values agreeing with each other and with a fabricated quotation, so nothing disagreed and nothing complained. Every companion has been drawing two extra skill points per level, forty over twenty levels. `skillPointAbility` is already "wisdom", so the plus-Wis half was right all along and only the base was wrong. FOUND BY WRITING THE COMPANION HARNESS Graham asked for on 18 September 2026, and only because its checks were transcribed from the printed page instead of from the module - a check taking the constant as its expected value would have agreed with the defect for ever.

fixes.name: Hand Crossbow
fixes.reason: RULING R6 OF THE BLOCK-15 AUDIT (pages 151-160, Graham 19 September 2026): follow the printed weapon groups. Page 157 lists the Bow group as 'Hand Crossbow, Heavy Crossbow, Light Crossbow, Composite Longbow, Composite Shortbow, Longbow, Shortbow, Repeater' and the Dart group as 'Blowgun, Dart, Javelin, Shuriken'. The pack gave the crossbows and the blowgun groups of their own (raised 3.215.0, never settled) because ammunition was matched on group; what a weapon fires is now its own field, `ammunitionFamily`, read by `weaponAmmunitionFamily` in module/combat/ammunition.mjs.

fixes.name: Nightsage
fixes.from:
The fragrant purple blossoms of this night-blooming wildflower are so deep in hue that they appear almost black.

When dried nightsage is lit on fire, it produces a thin but pleasant-smelling smoke almost like that produced by a stick of incense. A dose of nightsage burns for 10 minutes and can be extinguished and reignited for multiple uses (but it is always used in 1-minute increments, regardless of the actual time spent burning).

While nightsage burns, each corporeal undead creature within a 5-foot radius gains a +2-status bonus on saving throws against positive energy effects. Necromancers are fond of supplying their undead minions with small thimbles containing a burning stick of nightsage that can be worn while carrying out their commands. A moderate or stronger wind extinguishes a burning stick of nightsage.

Terrain: any jungles.
